💡 Key Takeaways
  • Employees of “Grand Theft Auto VI” developer Rockstar Games voted against union recognition this week.
  • 26 vote that included 1,544 staff members (93.2% voter turnout across the Rockstar Games workforce), 75.3% voted against Rockstar Game Workers Union’s recognition with the Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) and 24.7% voted in support.
  • As a result of the vote, Rockstar Games is not required to recognize the union and regularly engage in collective bargaining with reps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Employees of “Grand Theft Auto VI” developer Rockstar Games voted against union recognition this week.

In a Nov. 26 vote that included 1,544 staff members (93.2% voter turnout across the Rockstar Games workforce), 75.3% voted against Rockstar Game Workers Union’s recognition with the Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) and 24.7% voted in support.

As a result of the vote, Rockstar Games is not required to recognize the union and regularly engage in collective bargaining with reps. Related Stories ‘Summer Meadow’ Directors Confront 'Hypocrisy' in Films About Migrants: 'It’s as Though Black and Arab People Are Forbidden to Dream' All the 'GTA 6' Celebrity Cameos: Jeremy Irons, Janelle James, John Leguizamo, Chloe Fineman and More Vice City Residents.

Sources indicate that “For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for,” the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said in a statement. “Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of ‘Grand Theft Auto 6,'” Rockstar Games head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement.

Industry observers note that A Rockstar Games spokesperson added: “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.”.

See more gaming news from the week in the roundup below.

The wait for “Avengers: Doomsday” is almost over, and soon, fans can play in that world in addition to watching the story unfold.

It has been revealed that to celebrate the movie hitting theaters Dec. 18, Scopely, in collaboration with Marvel Games, is uniting “Monopoly Go!” with Marvel Studios’ highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday” for an all-fresh season of “Doomsday Go!”.

Sources indicate that this season, which runs Nov. 25 — Jan. 27, brings fresh shields, tokens and dice with richer animations and visual effects and visually enhanced super stickers and super tokens.

The “Doomsday Go!” album is packed with 23 unique sticker sets featuring Marvel Super Heroes from Thor and Iron Man to Deadpool, Wolverine, Spider-Man, the X-Men and more. Players can collect super hero team sets, follow story sets, explore whimsical designs and piece together puzzles as Tycoons build a collection worthy of the Marvel Universe.

Wargaming’s “World of Tanks” will feature actor Steve Buscemi as the star of its Holiday Ops 2027, the highly anticipated annual winter celebration across the video game franchise.

In a recent development, buscemi stars as Coldstone, an observant investigative reporter (and tank enthusiast) who is introduced in a upcoming short film released to promote the “World of Tanks” Holiday Ops season. When the regular anchor is unable to go on air, he takes over the live broadcast just as a series of holiday disasters begins to pile up on screen. Sensing a conspiracy and spotting clues others miss, Coldstone uncovers the truth and saves the holidays. Once the broadcast is over, Coldstone invites players into World of Tanks as a tank commander, ready to set assignments and share festive rewards.

“What I liked about Coldstone is that he doesn’t just go along with the story. He pays attention and has a real eye for detail,” Buscemi mentioned. “I hope World of Tanks players enjoy the retro style, humor, and holiday spirit in the film.”.

Lenny Kravitz has been revealed as the new Elusive Target in “HITMAN World of Assassination” reprising the role of his iconic “007 First Light” character, the Pirate King Bawma.

Per IO Interactive (the developer behind both the “Hitman” franchise and “007 First Light”), “In this latest mission, Agent 47 is deployed to Ambrose Island on the instructions of the Pirate King, Bawma. A former child soldier turned ruthless ruler of Aleph, Bawma was last seen in IO Interactive’s Game of the Year nominee 007 First Light, where he commands both fear and respect in equal measure. This time around, Bawma has a rather unconventional assignment for Agent 47, insisting on directing the operation himself and guiding 47 throughout the mission via in-ear dialogue. Once 47 tracks Bawma down through the ruins and jungles of Ambrose Island, it soon becomes clear that something far more valuable than a simple target is at stake. Lenny Kravitz lends both his voice and likeness to his reprisal of Bawma, and the mission brings a bright, upbeat tone and an easy-going holiday feel to World of Assassination.”.

The Battle of the Boroughs Minecraft Competition will return to New York City for the fifth consecutive year.

Hosted by Newly introduced York City Public Schools and the NYC Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment (MOME), the competition incentivizes students in grades 3-12 to build a more inclusive and sustainable culture while developing critical thinking, computer science, public speaking and problem-solving skills. This year’s prompt will challenge students to develop Minecraft builds that create a safer, more connected Penn Station neighborhood.

Recent findings suggest that submissions for elementary, middle and high school teams are now open on the New York City Public Schools website and close Jan. 6.

ITV Studios unveiled on Monday a faithful, nostalgia-packed “Roblox” experience based on the original 1960s TV series “Thunderbirds.”.

The game introduces a latest generation to the series by recreating the look and spirit of the show, from the famous launch sequences to the craft designs fans grew up with, all with a modern twist.

“Recreating Thunderbirds, such an iconic piece of British television and a treasured brand at ITV Studios, required immense care, passion and dedication,” Ashley Lewis, managing director of Metavision, noted. “By pairing the unmistakable DNA and enduring spirit of the 1960s original with Roblox’s rapidly evolving technical capabilities, we’ve been able to bring Tracy Island and its iconic rescues to life with truly impressive scale and fidelity. We hope we’ve created an authentic experience for long-standing fans while introducing a fresh generation to the excitement and imagination of Thunderbirds.”.

NASA’s Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, NASA's Voyager 1 has achieved another extraordinary milestone, becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth.
  • The historic moment occurred on November 18 at 2:16 a.m.
  • The achievement marks another remarkable chapter for a probe that has traveled farther than any other human-made object, survived decades beyond its original mission, and continues to explore a region of space that no spacecraft had previously entered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, NASA's Voyager 1 has achieved another extraordinary milestone, becoming the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth. After more than 49 years of traveling through space, humanity's most distant spacecraft is now approximately 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from home. At that distance, even a signal moving at the speed of light needs an entire day to make the journey.

The historic moment occurred on November 18 at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST). Scientists and engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, which is managed by Caltech, received a signal from Voyager 1 early Thursday, exactly 24 hours after the spacecraft reached the milestone.

The achievement marks another remarkable chapter for a probe that has traveled farther than any other human-made object, survived decades beyond its original mission, and continues to explore a region of space that no spacecraft had previously entered.

Voyager 1 Is Now 24 Light-Hours From Earth.

Astronomers often describe enormous cosmic distances in terms of how long light takes to travel them. A light-day represents the distance light covers in 24 hours, or roughly 16.1 billion miles.

Light moves through a vacuum at approximately 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) per second. To put Voyager 1's distance in perspective, sunlight passing Earth takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon. Reaching Neptune takes roughly four hours, while traveling from Neptune to Voyager 1 requires another 20 hours.

It has been revealed that even these enormous distances are small compared with those separating stars. A single light-year, the distance light travels in one year, measures approximately 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers).

Voyager 1's extraordinary distance also creates a major challenge for mission controllers. Sending a command to the spacecraft now requires 24 hours, and receiving a response takes another 24 hours. A complete exchange therefore spans two full days, even though the signals travel at the fastest speed possible.

In a recent development, the milestone comes as engineers investigate a communication problem. NASA has not received scientific or engineering data from Voyager 1 since November 14. However, the probe continues transmitting a carrier signal, the radio signal that normally carries information back to Earth. By tracking this signal and calculating the spacecraft's trajectory, mission specialists were able to verify that Voyager 1 had crossed the one light-day mark. Engineers are continuing to investigate why the expected data is not coming through.

A Historic Journey Beyond the Solar System's Planets.

Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, were launched in 1977 to take advantage of an unusual arrangement of the outer planets. The alignment allowed the spacecraft to use planetary gravity to travel from one destination to another, making an ambitious exploration mission possible.

Managed by JPL, the Voyagers became the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn. They also delivered the first high-resolution images of these distant planets, revealing extraordinary new details about their atmospheres, rings, and moons. Voyager 2 continued farther, becoming the first spacecraft to explore Uranus and Neptune up close.

Today, both probes are traveling through interstellar space, making them humanity's only spacecraft to have crossed into the region beyond the Sun's protective bubble. Their instruments continue monitoring changes in the Sun's magnetic field across immense distances, providing scientists with measurements that cannot be collected from Earth.

According to recent reports, "Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets," said Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. "But it went on to become central to NASA's fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun.".

"Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery," noted Dave Gallagher, JPL director. "Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. As NASA pushes toward new frontiers in human and robotic exploration, Voyager and the people behind its success continue to inspire us to reach farther and dream bigger.".

Voyager's Golden Record Carries a Message From Earth.

The Voyager spacecraft carry more than scientific instruments. Each also holds a Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph record containing images and sounds representing life on Earth. These recordings were designed as messages that an advanced extraterrestrial civilization might discover someday.

The records give the mission a purpose extending far beyond its scientific discoveries. Even after the spacecraft eventually lose the ability to communicate with Earth, they will continue traveling through space with a small collection of sights and sounds from the planet that debuted them.

It has been revealed that "Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, the Voyager mission continues to push the boundaries of human exploration. Its epic journey reflects the vision of Ed Stone, the Caltech physicist and JPL director who guided the mission for decades, and the curiosity and tenacity of generations of scientists and engineers who have carried that vision forward," mentioned Ray Jayawardhana, president, Caltech. "Beyond its immense contributions to science, Voyager also captures something profound about the human spirit. We may never know where its journey will ultimately lead, but it will venture on, an enduring affirmation that humanity was here and we yearned to explore.".

Exploring the Mysterious Region Beyond the Sun.

It has been revealed that voyager 1 is currently moving through space at approximately 38,000 mph (61,155 kph). In 2012, it became the first spacecraft to cross the boundary of the heliosphere, a vast region surrounding the Sun that is filled with particles and magnetic fields generated by our star.

In a recent development, this protective bubble helps shield the solar system from cosmic radiation arriving from elsewhere in the galaxy. Beyond its outer boundary lies interstellar space, where particles and magnetic fields from the broader galaxy become more dominant.

Voyager 2 followed a different route and crossed into interstellar space in 2018. Together, the probes are providing the first direct observations of conditions beyond the heliosphere.

Sources indicate that one of their most intriguing discoveries is that the Sun's effects do not simply disappear at the boundary. Its influence appears to extend much farther into interstellar space than scientists once understood, raising new questions about where the environment shaped by our star truly gives way to the surrounding galaxy.

Industry observers note that "The Voyagers are revolutionizing our understanding of interstellar space, a previously unexplored region outside the heliosphere," said Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist at JPL. "One substantial surprise is the extent to which our Sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1. Where does the Sun's influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may endure long enough to answer that question.".

How NASA Is Keeping Voyager 1 Alive After Nearly 50 Years.

Sources indicate that operating spacecraft built nearly half a century ago requires increasingly inventive engineering. Both Voyagers have experienced problems as their equipment ages, including clogged thrusters and a malfunctioning computer. NASA engineers have repeatedly developed solutions that allow the probes to continue working despite these setbacks.

Electricity has become one of the mission's greatest limitations. Earlier in 2026, engineers took a calculated risk by switching off three devices aboard Voyager 1 and replacing them with three alternatives that consume less power. This change was intended to help the spacecraft stretch its remaining energy supply.

Voyager 1 depends on a radioisotope thermal generator that is now approximately 50 years old. Often described as a nuclear battery, the device produces electricity by converting heat released during the radioactive decay of plutonium.

Industry observers note that as the radioactive material continues to decay, the available power gradually decreases. Both Voyager spacecraft lose approximately four watts of electrical output every year, forcing engineers to make difficult decisions about which systems can remain operational.

The latest conservation measures are expected to provide enough power to operate the spacecraft's current scientific instruments until at least the summer of 2027, when both probes will celebrate their 50th launch anniversaries.

One Day, Voyager 1 Will Become a Silent Messenger to the Stars.

In a recent development, maintaining contact across such staggering distances requires some of NASA's most powerful communications equipment. The agency relies on its Deep Space Network, a worldwide system of large radio antennas located at three facilities, to communicate with Voyager and other spacecraft traveling to and beyond the Moon.

It has been revealed that despite the enormous communication delay and the spacecraft's aging systems, engineers continue monitoring Voyager 1 daily and transmitting instructions every week. The mission remains an extraordinary demonstration of what long-term spacecraft engineering can achieve.

Recent findings suggest that "We listen to Voyager 1 every day and send commands to the spacecraft weekly. It just takes a little longer to communicate than it used to," mentioned Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL. "Even traveling at the speed of light, signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to reach us. One day in the future, when it can no longer communicate with Earth, Voyager 1 will become humanity's silent ambassador to the stars.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding.
  • In the snapshot, the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates.

Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding.

In the snapshot, the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission.

This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft at the moment resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles, Blue Moon and Starship, respectively.

In a recent development, to prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to blueprint and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

#150779. Rejecting cheap fabrics, higher prices: Why shoppers are asking for better clothes

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1282 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Rejecting cheap fabrics, higher prices: Why shoppers are asking for better clothes

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.
  • Recent findings suggest that the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.

Recent findings suggest that the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S. has shifted in recent years. In 2010, about 60% of clothing was predominantly made from cotton. Now, that total is around 45%, while predominantly synthetic fabrics such as polyester and nylon comprise the majority of imports.

Recent findings suggest that apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index. Since 2020, they have soared to record highs.

It's starting to change habits for consumers who are paying more for food, gas, rent and other staples. As shoppers shell out more for clothes, they're increasingly making sure the garments are worth the cost.

Consulting firm AlixPartners' 2026 Consumer Sentiment Index, which surveyed more than 9,000 shoppers, found that consumers are scrutinizing labels more closely and rejecting cheap materials sold at a premium.

"If it's not a natural material, a retailer brand who passes it off as it is, they're really becoming very low on consumers' minds," remarked Sonia Lapinsky, head of fashion at AlixPartners.

According to recent reports, fast fashion brands like Forever 21 and H&M exploded in popularity during the early 2000s and 2010s, bringing trendy clothing to shelves promptly at low prices. Then came ultra-fast fashion, with brands like Shein and Fashion Nova pumping out new garments at even quicker speeds and lower price points — made possible in part through the use of inexpensive, synthetic fabrics.

"We got to a point where the pendulum just swung too far in that direction. And we've actually begun to see a reversal," said U.S. Bancorp BTIG consumer analyst Janine Stichter. "Quality matters a lot more ... over the last three or four years than it has in the previous 10 or 20.".

But quality, which shoppers often tie directly to material, can come at a higher cost.

Sources indicate that the average unit price of apparel imported to the U.S. between January and August was $2.64 per square meter for garments that were predominantly synthetic fiber, like polyester and nylon, compared with $3.67 for items that were largely cotton, according to data from the U.S. Commerce Department's Office of Textiles and Apparel.

When comparing those 2026 figures to 2010, synthetic fiber apparel import costs have climbed around 11%, while cotton apparel costs have risen 21%.

"If you're appealing to a more value-sensitive customer, you either reduce the quality, or you negotiate with suppliers to try to share some of the cost or you maybe absorb the cost … and perhaps hope to crank a higher volume of product to make up for it," mentioned Bernstein Research senior retail analyst Aneesha Sherman.

Though polyester is cheaper, experts point out that's not necessarily a bad thing. It can help clothing hold its shape and wick away sweat.

It has been revealed that sherman believes the athleisure boom is a primary factor in the shift toward polyester. She said that from 2015 to 2025, sports apparel was growing at a 4.9% rate in the U.S., versus 2.6% for all apparel and footwear, according to Euromonitor data.

"There probably is some quality trade down as well happening there," Sherman mentioned. "But I think both these trends are conflated.".

Sources indicate that nonetheless, backlash to synthetic materials is growing. Gen Z has even repurposed the word "polyester" as an insult to mean generally low-quality or fake.

Concerns have also grown about the environment and human health surrounding petroleum-based clothing, as more research indicates microplastics can leach from polyester clothing when washed.

It's led consumers to reexamine what materials are in their clothing.

Recent findings suggest that apparel prices have risen coming out of the pandemic, as demand outpaced supply and allowed companies to raise prices, stated BTIG's Stichter. Tariffs and the Iran war followed, raising costs for businesses — and prices for consumers.

Petroleum is the basis of many synthetic fibers, and oil prices have skyrocketed since the start of the Iran war.

The same factors that helped drive up prices of clothing — Covid, tariffs and war — also affected clothing quality.

"Companies had to move around their supply chains in the post-Covid period," said Stichter. "They had to find ways to take costs out, and sometimes that meant using less expensive fabrics.".

Those factors compounded a more-than-decade-long shift away from manufacturing in China.

Sheng Lu, a fashion and apparel studies professor at the University of Delaware, whose research focuses on the economics of the global textile industry, said China's established history with clothing production means it has higher-skilled workers, state-of-the-art-equipment and better material management compared with emerging manufacturing destinations such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Cambodia.

"They mostly serve the value market and the mass market. And I think the reason why they're not ready to make higher-quality luxury and premium products really reflects the kind of skill sets you can expect when you source from these countries," stated Lu.

AlixPartners' Lapinsky mentioned these countries that manufacture at a lower cost sometimes have to still ship the raw materials from China, which can extend the timeline to make clothing. That means taking earlier bets on trends and then discounting if products don't sell well.

"If you have to mark down that product because the consumer doesn't want it as much, your net margin might actually be worse than if you were to just invest in quality in the first place," stated BTIG's Stichter.

And as material costs rise for synthetic fibers, Stichter also remarked she believes it could further influence companies to use more natural fabrics moving forward.

Companies prioritizing quality are winning in this environment.

Recent findings suggest that ralph Lauren's stock is up around 85% over the past two years. Around 90% of its apparel is primarily made of cotton, leather, wool, viscose, cashmere or silk, according to its 2026 sustainability report. In its fiscal 2026, the firm said it sold more products at full price and reduced markdowns.

Meanwhile, direct-to-consumer clothing brand Quince, which centers its brand identity around natural materials, reached a $10 billion valuation this year.

The brand jumped 16 spots to No. 3 for best resale value in online consignment retailer ThredUp's 2025 report. Organic cotton retailer Pact jumped 20 spots on that list to No. 8, illustrating the potential role materials are playing in brand recognition.

Alternatively, the 2026 AlixPartners report, which ranks sentiment for brands in different retail categories, found shoppers are viewing some fast fashion brands less favorably. Both Shein and Zara dropped three spots — to fifth and seventh place, respectively — in terms of sentiment in the young adult specialty category.

Shein passed higher tariff costs onto shoppers in 2025 and then blamed a sales slowdown on those higher prices. The ultra-fast fashion retailer saw its year-over-year share of U.S. apparel, accessories and footwear card spending decrease in the fourth quarter of 2025 and first two quarters of 2026, according to Consumer Edge.

Shein did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Though Zara fell in AlixPartners' Consumer Sentiment Index, it has continued to grow sales and profits year over year. Even so, Lapinsky remarked worsening consumer views are something to watch, even if the organization is doing well.

Sources indicate that "What we found over the years with this consumer sentiment index is that sometimes it will be a bit of a leading indicator of what's to come," mentioned AlixPartners' Lapinsky. "I'm not saying that this is going to be true for Zara, but I think that's one thing that we'll be watching as we look in the upcoming quarters and into 2027.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that british actor Arthur Conti is fresh off a whirlwind year.
  • “To play an iconic character that’s been played by many people before, and to get to give your own spin on it, is very exciting,” Conti tells The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom from London about what he’s been up to this year.
  • The 22-year-old actor is back in the U.K.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that british actor Arthur Conti is fresh off a whirlwind year. With roles in Mike Flanagan’s Carrie adaptation and the recently released Ebenezer, he’s been busy crafting fresh interpretations of well-known characters.

“To play an iconic character that’s been played by many people before, and to get to give your own spin on it, is very exciting,” Conti tells The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom from London about what he’s been up to this year.

The 22-year-old actor is back in the U.K. after over a month of press for Carrie and Ebenezer and a stint in Portland, Oregon. “It’s been a bit of a whirlwind, but it’s been very enjoyable,” he states. After a breakout performance in 2024’s Beetlejuice Beetlejuice, 2026 has been the actor’s biggest year to date between the two projects and a role in Jane Schoenbrun’s Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma. Related Stories TV Why Mike Flanagan Just Couldn't Kill Carrie White Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Slays $120M at Box Office as Franchise Heats Back Up.

It has been revealed that with Carrie, Conti stepped into the role of teen bully Billy Nolan, first played on screen by John Travolta in Brian De Palma’s 1976 film. Conti had read Stephen King’s novel but hadn’t seen De Palma’s film, which he stayed away from during filming. Conti’s Billy, while still one of the villains of the story, is different from Travolta’s take on the character. “I was worried that even inadvertently or subconsciously I would copy things about that performance, and I really wanted it to be all my own,” he states.

It has been revealed that ebenezer finds Conti stepping into the shoes of the titular character of Ebenezer Scrooge — well, the younger version of him anyway. The actor heard that Ti West would be making the film, and as a major fan, he sent in a self-tape. Much like with Carrie, he tried not to take too much inspiration from previous versions of the story, but there’s one adaptation that stands out.

“[The Muppets version] is probably the best one. I mean, it’s amazing, that film. Michael Caine gives such a genuinely brilliant, dramatic performance in that film against the Muppets,” he says. “He takes it so seriously, and that is the beauty of that film is that you’d think he was talking to John Gielgud, and he’s talking to Fozzy.”.

It has been revealed that despite The Muppets Christmas Carol being his main experience with the story beforehand, he did watch the 1951 film adaptation starring Alastair Sim as Scrooge. “I really liked,” he notes.

Below, the actor digs into his last year in roles, what he’s looking to do next and how he’d spend a perfect day in London.

I’m always curious, as someone who enjoys it — have you seen Carrie: The Musical?

We watched it. We saw a theater production on Granville Island in Vancouver. It was a youth theater production of Carrie: The Musical. [The cast of Carrie] all went to go and see it. Mike [Flanagan] actually put the cast of that production of Carrie in the show. They’re all at the prom. Throughout the show, they’re in the background at the school, which was really, really fun.

It has been revealed that how has the year been? You were busy with Carrie and now Ebenezer.

[Carrie] was my first big press tour. It was my first time doing a press junket and all of these things. It feels like the biggest thing that I’ve done so far [with] how much I’ve been promoting it. It was all incredibly exciting. [In Carrie,] I’m playing another character that has several sides to him, after [I did in] Beetlejuice. It’s another deceptively charming, manipulative character, which is interesting that I keep taking. (Laughs).

Where do you think that’s coming from?

Something about me, I don’t know. Something untrustworthy. Honestly, it is a treat to play characters like that because you get the chance to do multiple things at once, present a character that has many layers and is complex and isn’t wholly one thing or another. It was a great role. It was a really meaty role to sink my teeth into, and it was an honor to play a character of that literary significance. It was a privilege to be entrusted with that.

As an actor, are you drawn to characters that are different from you, then?

It’s nice to get outside of yourself — that’s part of the fun of it. Growing up, the films I was watching, I was a lot more drawn to flawed or strange or darker characters. I grew up watching Steve Buchemi in Fargo and Philip Seymour Hoffman in Punch-Drunk Love and Talented Mr. Ripley. Those are the kind of characters that I always really loved to watch.

The scope of the projects you had this year has been quite large. Are you drawn to that or looking to change it?

Sources indicate that you’re right. They are quite large-scale. I think I’m drawn to things that are a little out there and a little strange. Horror is one of the best genres to explore that area because it emboldens filmmakers to experiment and take risks and be a bit weird and a bit dreamlike. That’s why I gravitate towards horror a lot, and it’s probably what I watch the most of in the cinema.

Is that where you got your love for it? Were you major into horror as a kid?

In a recent development, I think so. It’s not horror, just things that are a little strange. My mom brought me up on Charlie Kaufman films. Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind is my mom’s favorite film, so I watched that quite early. Things that tap into that dreaminess and that weirdness and spookiness — that’s up my alley. But it would be a dream to do a Before Sunrise kind of thing, where it’s just two people talking for an hour and a half. I would love to do something like that next.

Is that what you’re looking to do going forward then?

It has been revealed that it could be anything. I really want to leave myself open. I would love to do something a little more scaled down, kind of dialogue-heavy thing. I could never have imagined the caliber of director and the caliber of actor that I’ve been working with. If I can only just continue to do that, I will be very lucky indeed. I’ve gotten to work with some of my absolute heroes, and that’s been wonderful. But I want to keep working in horror as well. Horror’s having a really exciting moment right now, especially young people in horror, with Obsession and Backrooms. I will stay as long as it’ll have me. Horror, fantasy — that’s what I grew up with, and I want to explore that more as well.

What does your ideal day off look like?

I would wake up at 10:30 a.m.-ish. I’m a very late-to-bed, late-to-rise kind of person in my free time. I’d wake up then; I’d get a coffee; I’d go for a walk. I have to do 10,000 steps a day. I’m like a dog. I have to be walked. Then I would go and see a movie. I would go to the cinema. I would probably go to the Prince Charles Cinema, which is my favorite in the world. I don’t know whether I’d see it on my own or with somebody else. I do go on my own to the cinema a lot. That’s one of my favorite ways to watch a film. Then I’d get a nice dinner. I might go shopping a little bit. I might go record shopping, go DVD shopping. Then I would go to the pub maybe, and then I would go to bed at 1 a.m. I’m being very specific with the times.

I’m unfamiliar with Prince Charles Cinema; why is that your favorite theater?

Just the vibe there, and the programming. There’s always something on there that’s worth seeing. I honestly have so much to thank that cinema for because the education in film that it has given me is just insane. I’ve seen so many films there for the first time. It’s one of the few places, in London especially, where you can see old films and cult films and things that don’t get screened very often. You can go and experience them in the theater, and that’s a very valuable thing. They were going to possibly get shut down, but they’ve just won the battle against the landlord or whatever. They’re going to be there for another 25 years. I’m very happy about that.

#150776. A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath

A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1786 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronomers have uncovered an extraordinary stellar collision in the neighboring Andromeda galaxy, where a smaller star spiraled into a gigantic supergiant and ultimately merged with it.
  • Researchers have nicknamed the resulting star Bao, describing it as potentially "rejuvenated" by the merger.
  • Recent findings suggest that observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope provided crucial evidence of what happened.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronomers have uncovered an extraordinary stellar collision in the neighboring Andromeda galaxy, where a smaller star spiraled into a gigantic supergiant and ultimately merged with it. The rare event, the first of its kind to be identified, left behind a single star that may have been given a upcoming lease on life.

Researchers have nicknamed the resulting star Bao, describing it as potentially "rejuvenated" by the merger. The smaller star was slightly less massive than our Sun, while its enormous companion was a swollen supergiant. The dramatic encounter took place near the outer edge of Andromeda and was investigated through a NASA-funded research effort.

Recent findings suggest that observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope provided crucial evidence of what happened. By combining Webb's findings with years of measurements from ground-based and space telescopes, scientists were able to reconstruct the stars' remarkable transformation.

"Stellar mergers are very, very difficult to observe in real time because they are hard to predict," said Viraj Karambelkar, the first author of a upcoming paper in Nature and a NASA Hubble Fellow at Columbia University in New York. "However, we noticed something unusual was going on in 2023 and continued to monitor the system to see what it would do. Then, in 2025, it erupted! Webb observed Bao only 47 days after the stars' eruption peaked, the earliest ever follow-up of an event like this. The telescope's data helped us characterize what the system looked like before, during, and immediately after the merger, which is absolutely mind-blowing.".

How a Giant Star Swallowed Its Companion.

For thousands of years, the two stars existed as a binary system, orbiting one another without merging. That long period of relative stability ended when the smaller star began brushing against the enormous outer atmosphere of its companion.

Once that interaction started, the process moved surprisingly rapidly. The two stars completed their "unification" after just seven additional orbits (about seven years). Previously observed mergers involving pairs of smaller stars had required thousands of orbits to reach the same outcome.

The speed of the final eruption also caught astronomers off guard.

According to recent reports, "We thought an outburst from such an extended star would take years," said co-author Nadia Blagorodnova, an associate professor at the University of Barcelona in Spain. "One day, its brightness started rising and within a week, it peaked!".

Scientists had already detected subtle warning signs before the eruption. As the smaller star moved through the giant's outer atmosphere, it disturbed the surrounding gas and began stripping away material, gradually changing the system's brightness.

"When a companion star begins to interact with the outer surface of the primary star, it produces a subtle effect -- a slow brightening, which we clearly saw in Bao's data," said co-author Kishalay De, an assistant professor at Columbia University in Fresh York. "As the companion continues its orbit, it keeps peeling off the primary star's outer layers, and that gas flows away into the surrounding space.".

A Violent Stellar Merger With More Than One Possible Outcome.

In a recent development, this kind of interaction is part of a process astronomers call common envelope evolution. It occurs when two stars become surrounded by a shared outer layer of gas, typically after one star expands enough to engulf its companion.

As the smaller star moves through that gas, resistance slows its orbit and drains away orbital energy. The companion can then spiral progressively deeper toward the center of the larger star.

It has been revealed that for Bao, the smaller star ultimately plunged inward and merged with the giant. Webb's observations provided the evidence needed to confirm that the stars had become one.

In a recent development, but such encounters do not always end with a merger. Sometimes, both stars survive, losing substantial amounts of material while emerging as two separate objects locked in much tighter orbits.

These surviving systems are important because they can eventually produce some of the universe's most extreme phenomena. Depending on how the stars evolve, they may become neutron stars or black holes, undergo violent supernovae, generate gravitational waves that ripple through space-time, or form rapidly rotating objects called millisecond pulsars.

Understanding common envelope evolution is therefore essential to explaining how many of these extraordinary cosmic objects come into existence.

Reconstructing the Collision With James Webb.

To understand exactly what happened to Bao, the researchers refined computer simulations of the two stars and compared the results with Webb's observations.

The telescope's mid-infrared measurements were particularly valuable because they revealed dust that the giant star had expelled over hundreds of years. Infrared light allows astronomers to study material that can be difficult to detect at visible wavelengths, offering clues about the system's history long before its final eruption.

According to recent reports, the simulations revealed that the larger star had been truly enormous. Before the merger, it was approximately seven times as massive as the Sun, had a radius 350 times larger, and shone with 18,000 times the Sun's brightness.

Those staggering proportions earned it the nickname "Big Bao.".

"It was an absolute beast of a star, completely outshining its companion in the data," mentioned co-author Karel Temmink, a Ph.D. student at Radboud University in Nijmegen, Netherlands, who led the simulations.

The researchers also calculated the mass of the smaller star for the first time. Nicknamed "Little Bao," it was likely somewhat smaller and dimmer than the Sun, with an estimated mass of (about 0.7 solar masses). In other words, it contained roughly 70% as much mass as our star.

At first, the simulations suggested that the smaller companion might have retained enough energy to "flee" the giant's gravitational grip and escape the encounter.

Further investigation, however, revealed a very different ending. Little Bao had been dragged deep into the core of Massive Bao, releasing an immense amount of energy as the two stars merged.

Their final encounter was "almost like a bomb exploding inside a living star," De said.

The merger has left astronomers with another key question: What is Bao like now?

It has been revealed that the surviving star contains the legacy of both original stars, but its final structure and mass distribution remain uncertain. Future observations will be needed to determine how its "heft" settles as the newly merged object evolves.

Years of Telescope Observations Reveal the Warning Signs.

One reason this discovery is so valuable is that scientists had been watching Bao long before its dramatic eruption.

Although Webb supplied crucial information about the amount of material expelled and how efficiently the common envelope process unfolded, the team also drew on ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared observations from multiple observatories. Together, these measurements provided a detailed record of the system's changing behavior as the merger approached and unfolded.

The researchers had even published an earlier study shortly before the stars erupted. (In fact, they published their first paper right before the eruption in 2025.).

The first major clue appeared in February 2023, when astronomers examining archived observations from NASA's retired NEOWISE (Near-Earth Object Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer) mission noticed a star whose brightness was behaving unusually.

Earlier records indicated that the object had maintained a steady luminosity before 2018. Its later variations suggested that something significant was beginning to change.

Recent findings suggest that by September 2024, observations from the Wide-field Infrared Transient Explorer (WINTER) showed further evidence of activity. The system was growing brighter and releasing dust into the surrounding space.

Another important development came in July 2025, when NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) happened to observe Bao during a routine sky survey.

The telescope detected a striking change: Bao was rapidly fading in visible light while simultaneously becoming brighter in infrared light. This unusual combination provided another sign that the system was undergoing a major transformation.

According to recent reports, then, on October 17, 2025, the Zwicky Transient Facility detected the eruption. The observations revealed a sudden surge in brightness accompanied by a dramatic increase in temperature.

Scientists rapidly arranged additional observations to capture the unfolding event. In November 2025, NASA's now-retired Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and NOIRLab's Gemini North telescope in Hawaii supplied valuable new measurements.

Webb joined the effort on December 24, 2025, through an urgently approved Director's Discretionary Time program. This special observing opportunity allowed the telescope to examine the aftermath while the system was still undergoing rapid changes.

A New Window Into the Lives and Deaths of Stars.

The successful investigation of Bao, officially designated AT 2025abao, represents an important advance in the study of stellar mergers.

Rather than trying to reconstruct a cosmic event that occurred hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years earlier, astronomers were able to observe and analyze the process as it happened.

That timing made it possible to measure how efficiently the common envelope interaction transferred energy and expelled material from the system. Such measurements can help researchers improve their models of how binary stars evolve and what determines whether they merge or survive.

The discovery also arrives at an especially promising time for astronomy.

NASA's recently launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is preparing to carry out extensive publicly available surveys that could reveal many more unusual stellar events.

Recent findings suggest that one of its major observing programs, the Galactic Bulge Time-Domain Survey, will repeatedly monitor large numbers of stars, helping astronomers identify objects whose brightness or appearance changes over time. These temporary or changing phenomena, known as transient events, may include additional systems undergoing transformations similar to Bao's.

With more discoveries and coordinated follow-up observations, researchers could gain a much clearer understanding of how often stars engulf their companions and what happens afterward.

"There's going to be a large influx of similar discoveries just ahead," Karambelkar said.

The research received partial funding through NASA's Astrophysics Data Analysis Program.

Industry observers note that the James Webb Space Telescope, the largest and most powerful space observatory ever rolled out, supports the work of thousands of astronomers around the world. Its scientific mission includes investigating objects within our solar system, exploring planets orbiting distant stars, and studying the formation, structure, and evolution of the universe to better understand our cosmic origins and place within it.

Webb is an international collaboration led by NASA in partnership with ESA (European Space Agency) and CSA (Canadian Space Agency).

#150774. Industry News: Record Store Day Black Friday’s Most Wanted, 2026: Beatles, Noah Kahan, Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Sombr, Billy Joel, Katseye and Other Vinyl Must-Finds

Industry News: Record Store Day Black Friday’s Most Wanted, 2026: Beatles, Noah Kahan, Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Sombr, Billy Joel, Katseye and Other Vinyl Must-Finds

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Variety

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, record Store Day is back in black.
  • Our best guess is that there will not be utter pandemonium in the indie shops or in the lines outside this Black Friday morning, if only because of the lack of a Taylor, Olivia or Billie title this time.
  • That stated, boomers are still gonna boom, and they, Gen-X-ers, millennials and others who have a taste for classic rock, soul and jazz — meaning every generation, really — will find something to salivate over in a list of vintage material that includes Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Joni Mitchell, Miles Davis, Billy Joel, Bill Withers, Art Blakey and even a collectible from the Beatles that was added to the list after it was first declared in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic.

In a recent development, record Store Day is back in black. As you likely already know, RSD is a semiannual holiday for vinyl hounds, with the Black Friday edition being a less jam-packed adjunct to the primary event in April — meaning that, this year, for instance, there are “only” 188 titles being released, almost exactly half of the 355 exclusives that were put on sale in the spring event. Even with that lesser amount of limited-edition discs going out onto the shelves, there is truly something for everybody in this list. Or, to put it another way: If you can’t find anything that grabs you in this lineup, then, to quote Leonard Cohen, you don’t really care for music, do ya?

Our best guess is that there will not be utter pandemonium in the indie shops or in the lines outside this Black Friday morning, if only because of the lack of a Taylor, Olivia or Billie title this time. Which does not mean that there will not still be a healthy contingent of young people joining the veteran vinyl geeks in the checkout lines. In an interview published earlier in the week in Variety, RSD co-founder Michael Kurtz said that the majority of customers for Record Store Day events are under 35. That may continue to be the case as this one has titles from hot and/or younger-skewing artists or franchises including Noah Kahan, Katseye, Sombr and the “Wicked” and “Kpop Demon Hunters” films.

That stated, boomers are still gonna boom, and they, Gen-X-ers, millennials and others who have a taste for classic rock, soul and jazz — meaning every generation, really — will find something to salivate over in a list of vintage material that includes Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Joni Mitchell, Miles Davis, Billy Joel, Bill Withers, Art Blakey and even a collectible from the Beatles that was added to the list after it was first declared in October.

If you want to see the entire list of 188 vinyl releases (a few of which are also having CD editions made available for the occasion) scroll all the way down. But first, if you will, look at our annotated list of 27 of the titles that we consider most covetable, ranging from Carly Rae Jepsen and Cher EPs to a 10,000 Maniacs boxed set to an expanded version of NRBQ’s classic Christmas album.

14,500 copies on 4x LP; 3,700 copies on 2x CD; black vinyl.

According to recent reports, springsteen buffs will not always agree on favorite individual highlights from his and the band’s 50-year-plus history, but it’s hard to imagine a single fan not considering the “Born to Run” era to be peak form. or not taking a serious interest in this rendering of a long and loose Fresh Year’s Eve concert at the close of 1975. The only question might be which physical format you want it in, since Sony is offering it for Record Store Day Black Friday in both LP and CD form. The much greater amount of vinyl pressed indicates an obvious consumer preference for vinyl nowadays, but with a concert this length, some may reconsider whether they want to flip sides seven times to get it all and opt for compact disc. Whether you pick up a vinyl slipcase or CD jewel box, there are succinct but sweet liner notes from Erik Flannigan, who points out that, yes, that is the band (except for Bruce) decked out in tuxedos in the photographs in the packaging. Good thing any formality about this wonderful show ends there.

10,000 copies of vinyl 12-inch EP; Alpenglow-colored vinyl.

According to recent reports, kahan’s exclusive releases have been among the biggest draws at many recent Record Store Days, which is no surprise, given the ongoing presence of two of his studio albums in the top 10 and stadium tours that sell out instantaneously. Fans will already be familiar with the four songs on this EP — “Lighthouse,” “Staying Still,” A Few of Your Own” and “Orbiter” — since they first appeared as bonus tracks on a digital deluxe edition of his smash “The Great Divide” album (and “Orbiter” is a proper single). But having the four tracks partitioned off into their own separate physical release will be irresistible to diehard stickheads.

It’s not like you’re going to get any songs here that you didn’t already get on the recent “Rubber Soul” 60th anniversary super-deluxe edition… or, for that matter, that you haven’t had access to since 1966. But then, that’s the point: This single LP is a recreation of the exact album that U.S. Beatles fans got in ’66, down to the original stereo mix. But that’s been out of print for a long time… and has never been uin print as a gold-colored record, which is the main novelty here. The good news for Beatles collectors is that it’s been pressed in numbers that fall at the very top end of pressings for Record Store Day; the bad news is that 15,000 still won’t last long.

9,400 copies on 3x vinyl; 2,700 copies on 2x CD; vinyl color is crystal blue curaçao.

Sources indicate that the Prince estate is really making the most out of the fact that it had a pro-shot film of Prince’s six-month 2006-7 residency in Las Vegas in the can. A film of “3121 Las Vegas Live” will briefly hit the big screen in early December, followed by a Blu-Ray edition for home consumption. In the meantime, if you want a physical manifestation of just the music, Record Store Day participant shops are the place to go. The performance captured here starts at a slow simmer but quickly heats up. Suffice it to say that, after hearing this purely audio version, I’ll be lined up for the movie.

Industry observers note that every time there is a upcoming CD boxed set in the ongoing series of Joni Mitchell archival anthologies, a single live performance from that collection gets broken out to have its own separate LP edition for Record Store Day. No complaints at all about that. This ’72 concert is all Joni, accompanying herself on guitar, piano or dulcimer, all the way to a closing “Circle Game” that does have her suddenly surrounded by a chorus of famous and unfamous friends. Some will prefer Mitchell in her purest early-ish form here, and some may prefer the big band era that followed. But hearing the purity of that voice with an emphasis on the then-recent “Blue” and then-forthcoming “For the Roses” is a knockout experience. The only thing more you could wish for is a gatefold jacket instead of putting both discs in a single sleeve (the product description promises gatefold, but it’s not), or liner notes, but it’s still a handsome-looking as well as -sounding package.

It has been revealed that the last Billy Joel live album, released for Record Store Day Black Friday 2025, was “Live From Long Island,” pressed in a quantity of 1,500 copies — and fans are still pissed about that. (Resale copy prices are not completely exorbitant, but they do go for more than $100.) Fortunately, the record company got the message and is putting three times that many of this followup on sale, 4,600, although that still may not completely sate the market for live Joel. It’s a spirited set, from a hyperactive “Angry Young Man” opening forward, recorded Dec. 5, 1976 at Connecticut College for a TV special. It includes 15 never-before-released tracks from either the original live highlights or a followup that was done to get better takes for the special. The blurb on the back cover promises that four more tracks will be included in a “Turnstiles” 50th anniversary boxed set coming out next year. But few Joel fans will complain about that wait given the wealth of heretofore unreleased music here.

Sombr: 7,500 copies on silver vinyl.

Boone: 5,000 copies on black and white galaxy vinyl.

Recent findings suggest that the Sombr and Benson Boone releases are very similar, in that each is a first-time vinyl issue of the EP that started their major-label careers before they broke a lot bigger with a full album that followed. Bot EPs are also mellower than some of the hit music that followed for these artists — Sombr lives up to his name more here. His EP, at four tracks, is less expansive than Boones, which runs to eight songs, and comes with a 12-by-24 insert that has a poster image on one side and lyrics on the other. Apart from their musical merits, both discs just look fab, pulled out of their sleeves and placed into the wild.

Withers: 2,600 copies on LP; 1,300 copies on CD; LP is black vinyl.

Various artists/Sweet Relief: 1,200 copies.

It has been revealed that now here’s an unofficial two-fer anyone should think about picking up and turning into a double feature, even if their simultaneous release, coming from different labels, may be coincidental. First, there’s Withers’ own 1974 performance, captured for British TV. You can tell the audio is unedited: Withers is heard telling the studio audience that some of his band members are out sick, and in one case restarting a speech. The relaxed feel carries over to the superlative songs. Meanwhile, I have to give an even more enthusiastic endorsement to a double-LP tribute album put together as a benefit for the Sweet Relief Foundation that includes all-new tracks. I was hoping the great Chris Pierce — one of the closest things we have to a modern-day Withers right now — would be one of the artists chosen, and to my sweet relief, he was, contributing “Better Off Dead.” There are also choice cuts from Rickie Lee Jones, Lady Blackbird, Marilyn McCoo and Billy Davis Jr., Ben Harper and others who know how to mix their own spin on things with takes that feel faithful to Withers’ vibe.

2,600.copies of six-LP boxed set; multiple vinyl colors.

Rhino has gotten in the habit of issuing one complete boxed set per RSD event for a renowned artist from the Warner-Elektra catalog of riches, from John Prine to Devo. This one for 10,000 Maniacs, composed of all the albums the group put out before Natalie Merchant split to go solo in 1993, is being seen by fans as a very necessary corrective to the fact that a lot of that stuff has been out of print on vinyl forever. Four studio albums are joined by the pre-fame compendium “Hope Chest” and a newly assembled rarities disc full of delectable covers. Merchant is credited with helping oversee the package, including the design of the physical elements, although the liner notes (which are very good) do not include interviews with her or any of the bandmates who continue to carry on without her. It’s worth noting that all of the albums included except the rarities LP are due to be issued individually early next year, if it’s just one or two you need to pick up. But as a fan from their earliest major-label days, I couldn’t imagine not getting the whole thing right now. A matter of curiosity: All of the box and LP packaging here changes the band’s name to Ten Thousand Maniacs from 10,000 Maniacs (although the numerical usage pops up in the liner notes). Some elements of the album cover art have been changed, along with the band-name logos — it has to be a Merchant thing. But if you pick up the individual issues in a few months, apparently the name and artwork will be as we remember them. (The fact that the albums in this box have different covers is further cemented by the lack of barcodes.) Those peculiarities aside, t’s a great trip down maniacal memory lane.

It has been revealed that jepsen has been nothing but prolific in this era, first issuing “Day and Night” as a hefty double-album, then adding eight additional tracks onto the original 24 for a deluxe edition, “Day and Night (Continued).” that runs to an hour and 55 minutes of material. Some things may be more easily digested in smaller chunks, of course, and this EP — also titled “Day and Night (Continued)” — breaks out those eight fresher tracks and gives them their first appearance in a physical format. Plus, you get still more from her photo shoot at Eagle Rock’s Casa Bianca, the best pizza joint in L.A., and if that’s not reason enough to pick it up, you’ve got eight more.

According to recent reports, the previous RSD exclusive editions of the “Wicked” and “Wicked: For Good” sold out so swiftly, I never did actually catch a glimpse of either of them in my many store visits. That will probably prove true for this combined set that packages both soundtracks together in a 4-LP set in a slipcase with a poster. (The track list, if accurate as rendered online, leaves out the bonus track that was added onto the original RSD “Wicked” matter.) Good luck hunting this down, unless it turns out every franchise fan was sated by the previous two releases after all, which isn’t likely. It’s gonna be popular.

3,300 2x LP copies; black vinyl.

The first of several releases we’ll mention here produced by “jazz detective” Zefv Feldman is a welcome incursion into the wonderful world of Blakey. It comtbines two previously unreleased performances in Paris, the first from 1963 and sporting famous players like Freddie Hubbard and Wayne Shorter, the second with a different ensemble in ’68. “Moons” were on the band leader’s mind, as the collection includes the two major musical moon shots of the era, “Blue Moon” and “Moon River.” The latter opens the collection and might give Henry Mancini a heart attack if he were still around to have one — it’s like “Moon River” on amphetamines (not speaking literally, friends, just figuratively), and it’s quite a fantastic flood. The liner notes booklet is copious as with almost any Feldman-related release, and even though a CD edition will follow for the general market in a week, it’s always worth picking up the limited-edition vinyl versions of these releases just for the larger type and photographs. And, sure, the wide-open grooves, too.

5,000 copies of 2x LP; on “Third Pyramid Pink” vinyl.

I would have taken an interest in a B-52s live set anyway, but this one turns out to be particularly a wowser because of the addition of a three-man horn section that really helps some of the songs rock in an augmented way. Fans may already know this Roseland Ballroom NYC ’82 performance from when it was included in the “Ancient Culture: Mesopotamia Revisited” set, but for those of us who didn’t have that, or anyone who did but just likes a good breakout, it’s a delightful revelation of the band at its early ’80s peak.

3,500 copies of 12-inch vinyl EP; red vinyl.

Cher had not released any original material in many years until she came back with a Christmas project that included some songs newly written to add to the holiday tuneage canon. With this EP spinoff, the emphasis is on the dance-ier chestnuts, including three different mixes of “DJ Play a Christmas Song” and an added duet with Kelly Clarkson. The lady-in-red cover shot is different from any previous artwork in her Christmas-music campaign, too.

5,000 copies of single-sided EP.

We were not able to preview this particular release, so we cannot vouch for what the “dance break” versions of three of Katseye’s most popular songs sound like — “Debut,” “Gnarly” and “Gabriela.” But we can tell you the way it will fly off the shelves will be gnarly indeed. All three mixes are congregated on one side of the vinyl, with a mystery etching on the other. Each copy is said to includes two out of six “randomly selected unique photocards,” so fans will be figuring out how to get around the one-copy-per-customer rule in most stores, as if this needed an incentive to sell out faster.

2,600 copies of 2x LP; black vinyl.

Industry observers note that another archival production from Zev Feldman, who is stretching out from being seen as “just” a jazz guy with his Bobby Womack and Marianne Faithful releases this Record Store Day. Womack can also stretch out, as it turns out, with two numbers in this live set that go past the 12-minute mark, “You’re Welcome, Stop on By” and “Communication” are both over 12 minutes long. Recorded in Paris in 1976, where the liner notes say he was having a higher profile at the time than in the U.S., this collection feels essential as a revelation of just what an expansive showman he was as well as crafter of classic soul singles.

10,000 copies; “Derpy Sussie Splatter” vinyl.

According to recent reports, the hunt for “Kpop Demon Hunters” collectibles never stops. Record Store Day just had dual editions of the soundtrack that were quick and easy sellouts, but that could hardly stand in the way of yet another version — and surely not the last — this one featuring fresh art created by official “Demon Hunters” production designer Mingjue Helen Chen and visual development artist Marion Bordeyne. We’ll let the product description do the rest of the talking: “This Derpy Sussie Splatter vinyl includes exclusive holographic art on both the front cover and triple gatefold, 3 of 6 mini inserts, 1 of 3 holographic mini inserts, a sticker sheet, and an oversized poster.” You might have to take their word for it since it won’t be surprising if most or all of the copies are gone by the time you get your lazy post-Thanksgiving butt to the shop.

Sax man Getz is the only one with his name above the title on this release, but for the first three of its six sides, legendary guitarist João Gilberto is his equal costar. Together, they recreate the magic they’d made together in a historic studio teaming in one of the few live shows they did together to follow that. All the music here was previously released by Resonance more than a decade ago, but this three-LP set for the first time combines two albums — one of Getz with Gilberto in SF, one without — into an exemplary single package (and the Getz-only half of the equation never made it onto vinyl before). The multiple interviews or essays in the copious liner notes even include a sizable explanation of the bossa nova craze that finds a kind of quiet culmination here.

Recent findings suggest that fountains of Wayne’s final album before their breakup sometimes gets undervalued because it’s their least comical, most sober outing, perhaps reflecting the more dominant influence of Chris Collingwood, versus the wryer touch favored by Adam Schlesinger, who’d run the show more on the preceding record. Regardless, there’s wit enough here, along with some of the band’s starker songs. It’s been challenging for FoW fans to complete their vinyl collections, since this fast went out of print after a single pressing in 2001. Even now, 2,000 is not a lot, but it’ll be at least enough to satisfy some of us who never stopped believing that this brilliant group had it going on.

In a recent development, this is the “Bitches Brew”-era Miles who took free jazz into the land of psychedelia, if you hadn’t already guessed that from the cover art by his favorite cover painter in the ’60s, Mati Klarwein. It might as well have been recorded at the Fillmore, even though Davis actually had his all-star quintet (Wayne Shorter, Chick Corea, Dave Holland and Jack DeJohnette) in Copenhagen for a TV taping. The music has previously been heard on a DVD and on a one-time vinyl pressing of just a few hundred copies, but this mastering is remarked to be a revelation even for the relatively small number of cultists who’ve already heard this dynamic performance in some form.

3,500 copies; on “Pawn Shop Patina”-colored vinyl.

As the title and cover hint, this is a collection of cover songs these Dolls have done over the years, and what great taste they’ve had in other bands, as evidenced in a collection that runs from the Plimsouls’ “A Million Miles Away” to the Kinks’ “Catch Me Now, I’m Falling,” with stops for Tom Petty, INXS, Prince and… Supertramp! (A CD and digital release will follow a week after this vinyl exclusive.).

5,000 copies; 3D zoetrope picture-disc vinyl.

We did not get a review copy of this, but we’re going to guess from the product description alone that it might be fun, with or without actually listening to what’s in the grooves, just from looking at them. “Zoetrope” discs have been a thing for a while, turning vinyl into animation, but this is the first one we can recall seeing that is billed as a 3D zoetrope disc, with cardboard glasses to put on to enjoy the effect. We look forward to hearing whether the effect of watching that is as mind-bending as the Gizzard boys’ music typically is, and what substances it is best combined with.

1,800 copies on three-sided 2x LP set; black vinyl.

Sources indicate that we’re still morning Faithful’s passing, so it’s moving to hear her in her prime, or one of her primes, in a performance captured in 1983, after a comeback run of three acclaimed albums on Island, including of course “Broken English.” The tape of the D.C. set ends with the title track from that latter album and is missing a few final songs from the actual performance, so it’s spread across three sides and the fourth is devoted to an etching of a William Blake quote in concentric-circle script.

2,215 copies of six-45-rpm-singles boxed set; different marbled color variations.

Jazz Dispensary dispenses something worth picking up for every single RSD edition, and this time they’ve eschewed the usual single-LP compilation format to put out a box of singles. It comes in a candy-style box, with six different vintage singles in different but equally delicious-looking colors, plus some glow-in-the-dark 45 adapters as a bonus. As usual, even though the description calls these “jazz,” the music therein leans more toward the funk side of the fence, from Eddie Jefferson’s honestly groovy “Psychedelic Sally” to Patrice Rushen’s kinda-weird “Kickin’ Back.” Obscure but charming singles from Rusty Bryant, Idris Muhammad, Pleasure and Johnny Hammond are also represented. Will you play these a lot, or easily find shelf space for an odd-shaped package? Probably no in both cases, yet it’s kind of irresistible as a hep novelty package nonetheless.

1,200 copies; opaque green vinyl.

According to recent reports, what could be better for celebrating the season than NRBQ’s 1978 “Merry Christmas From NRBQ” EP? Very possibly, a modern expansion of that project that extends it to 19 tracks, 10 of them making their vinyl debut, one (the closing “Auld Lang Syne”) getting its premiere altogether. We weren’t able to preview this package to tell you whether they do or don’t rock out the newly added “Jesus Loves Me” and “The Christmas Song,” but we hope to score a copy and fill in that part of the NRB-FAQ.

Freigang banned — Germany star to miss 2027 World Cup

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Laura Freigang is set to miss next year's women's World Cup in Brazil after being suspended for missing doping tests, the German Football Association (DFB) noted in a statement on Thursday.
  • Freigang, who has played 45 matches for Germany and scored 17 goals, will be suspended until October 7, 2027 after reaching a settlement with the DFB, the World Anti-Doping Agency and Germany's National Anti-Doping Agency.
  • "It's vital to me to emphasize once again that I was never suspected of doping," Freigang mentioned in a statement on Instagram.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laura Freigang is set to miss next year's women's World Cup in Brazil after being suspended for missing doping tests, the German Football Association (DFB) noted in a statement on Thursday.

Freigang, who has played 45 matches for Germany and scored 17 goals, will be suspended until October 7, 2027 after reaching a settlement with the DFB, the World Anti-Doping Agency and Germany's National Anti-Doping Agency. The suspension is for the next 16 months as it began retroactively on June 8, 2026, when she was notified by the DFB, and prohibits Freigang from playing for club or country.

"It's vital to me to emphasize once again that I was never suspected of doping," Freigang mentioned in a statement on Instagram.

According to recent reports, "My agreement to a settlement does not mean that I share all the assessments of my case. The past few months have been extremely difficult for me. Another legal process would have entailed significant financial, mental, and emotional strain. This is why I decided to take this path, in the hope of finding some peace, clarity and perspective for myself," she added.

"It was never my intention to let it get this far. Sports have defined my life since I was little. It breaks my heart that, for now, I won't be able to step onto the field, help my team, or live the daily life that I love so much.".

According to recent reports, this brings to a close a case that has been ongoing for months. The 28-year-old had been accused of not being where she mentioned she would be for a doping control on three occasions between March 2025 and February 2026.

In June, Freigang explained missing the tests "were not deliberately avoided appointments but inconsistencies or misunderstandings in the comprehensive details that have to be updated daily and which we as national team players have to enhancement in the system on a daily and hourly basis.".

The ban ends her World Cup hopes, something the DFB has also acknowledged.

Sources indicate that "We are simply so sorry for Laura on a personal level because of this situation. The past few weeks have been very stressful for her," said DFB Sporting Director Nia Künzer. "We hold her in high regard both as a player and as a person, and — as we have done in recent weeks — we will continue to stay in touch with her and support her as best we can.".

The situation also puts her future at her club, Eintracht Frankfurt, into question. Freigang's contract runs until June next year.

"The agreement that has now been reached provides clarity and planning certainty through a process that is unique to Eintracht Frankfurt — for us as a club, but above all for Laura," said Katharina Kiel, Frankfurt's director of women's football.

The club and Freigang, who has played 180 Bundesliga games in her career, are now set to enter talks to determine the shape of her contract moving forward.
