A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1124 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has made an unexpected discovery in our own solar system.
  • The achievement is particularly remarkable given that Euclid was built to capture detailed images of distant galaxies rather than track rapidly moving objects such as comets.
  • A Mysterious Streak Reveals a Newly introduced Comet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has made an unexpected discovery in our own solar system. Images captured between September 16 and 24, 2026, revealed a previously unknown comet, the first discovered by the mission.

The achievement is particularly remarkable given that Euclid was built to capture detailed images of distant galaxies rather than track rapidly moving objects such as comets. The speed with which researchers identified and confirmed the discovery demonstrates that Euclid can detect new comets while they are still relatively far from the Sun. This capability could eventually help identify a target for ESA's upcoming Comet Interceptor mission.

A Mysterious Streak Reveals a Newly introduced Comet.

Mikko Pöntinen, a PhD student at the University of Helsinki, made the discovery with the Solar System Objects Science Working Group of the Euclid Consortium. Pöntinen developed specialized software to detect and track small solar system objects appearing in the telescope's images.

Industry observers note that "I was excited to see my software flag a 'streak' smeared across several images -- the result of a fast-moving object. By predicting its position I could identify it in other images, in total finding it in five image sets. Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas.".

The object appeared in a region of the sky known as the 'Euclid Deep Field North'. Over several days, the telescope captured it in five separate fields of view, taking between two and four exposures of each field for a total of 16 exposures.

According to recent reports, after searching catalogs of known asteroids and comets without finding a match, Pöntinen submitted the observations to the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center (MPC) as a potential newly introduced comet. The report enabled astronomers using telescopes on Earth to carry out additional observations. On October 8, the MPC officially confirmed the discovery. The comet has been designated C/2026 S1 (Euclid).

A Comet on an Extraordinary Orbit.

The newly discovered comet is approximately 1.3 billion kilometers (about 800 million miles) from Earth. That distance is comparable to the distance from the Sun to a point somewhere between the orbits of Jupiter and Saturn.

However, the comet is traveling well outside the relatively flat plane in which the planets orbit the Sun. It is right now positioned almost directly above the Sun, following a sweeping path over the solar system that will take thousands of years to complete.

Industry observers note that the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center (MPC) serves as the central international hub for observations of asteroids and comets. It gathers data from observers around the world to verify discoveries, determine orbital paths, and assign official designations. As additional observations become available, astronomers will be able to calculate the orbital period of C/2026 S1 (Euclid) more precisely.

Why Euclid Rarely Discovers New Comets.

It has been revealed that although Euclid has spotted comets before, all of them had already been discovered. Several aspects of the telescope's design and observing strategy make finding previously unknown objects within our solar system especially difficult.

Euclid intentionally avoids the region of the sky surrounding the plane of the solar system, where large numbers of asteroids and comets can be found. Dust concentrated in this region produces unwanted light that could interfere with the telescope's sensitive observations of the distant universe.

It has been revealed that the spacecraft also follows a 'step-and-stare' observing strategy, typically imaging each section of the sky only once. This means researchers cannot readily direct Euclid back toward a newly detected comet to gather more information about it.

Identifying objects within our solar system is nevertheless an notable part of Euclid's scientific work. Researchers must account for everything appearing in its images so that unrelated features, including comet trails and unwanted light, can be removed without compromising the accuracy of its galaxy measurements.

"Very few comets are expected to be discovered by Euclid so it was a happy coincidence that the combination of the comet's orbit and Euclid's scanning over those days captured the object in multiple images," says Bruno Altieri, Euclid Archive Scientist, and part of the discovery team.

Preparing for a Future Comet Encounter.

In a recent development, euclid's unexpected discovery also provides valuable experience for scientists working on ESA's future Comet Interceptor mission. Although the newly identified comet is not an appropriate destination for the spacecraft, the successful detection and rapid notification process demonstrates how the two missions could work together to identify potential targets.

"While this particular comet is not a suitable candidate for Comet Interceptor, the process of discovery and alert gives us a real test case for how our two mission teams will coordinate in the future. And we are of course happy to have discovered a previously unknown comet for the Solar System community to follow-up on," adds Valeria Pettorino, Euclid Project Scientist.

Ancient Remnants of the Solar System.

Comets are ancient bodies composed of ice and dust that remain from the formation of our solar system approximately 4.6 billion years ago. Most originate in the distant Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud, regions located beyond the orbits of the outer planets (interstellar comets come from other solar systems).

Industry observers note that as a comet approaches the Sun, increasing temperatures cause its ice to turn directly into gas. Escaping gas and dust form a glowing, fuzzy cloud known as a 'coma,' as well as an extended tail.

Because comets native to our solar system have remained relatively unchanged since their formation, they preserve valuable evidence of the materials and environmental conditions that existed when the planets were taking shape. Studying these ancient objects may also help scientists understand the origins of Earth's water and the chemical building blocks of life.

Euclid's Hunt for Dark Matter and Dark Energy.

The primary goal of the Euclid mission is to uncover how dark matter and dark energy influence the visible universe. During its six-year survey, the space telescope will examine the shapes and movements of billions of galaxies at distances reaching up to 10 billion light-years.

The comet discovery was reported on behalf of the Solar System Objects Science Working Group of the Euclid Consortium by M. Pöntinen, A. A. Nucita, A. Franco, M. Granvik, B. Altieri, S. Kruk, B. Y. Irureta-Goyena and B. Carry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ukrainian skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych has welcomed a move by the European Union to take a tougher stance on Russian athletes competing in the 27-member bloc.

In a recent development, heraskevych is one of the most outspoken critics of Russia's reintegration into international sport. He made headlines at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan-Cortina when he was disqualified for his helmet honoring Ukrainian athletes killed in the war with Russia.

On Monday, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed banning Russian athletes from competing under their own flag at sports competitions within the European Union and urged member states to consider denying visas in such cases.

"Sports events cannot be a forum for propaganda activities," she mentioned.

In an interview with DW, Heraskevych described the EU move as coming "better late than never.".

"We waited a long time for this backlash," he stated at the International Bobsleigh and Skeleton Federation World Cup in Altenberg, Germany, his first competition since the Winter Olympics.

"I'm really happy to see that people start to care about sports and they understand the value of sports as a huge platform," he added.

Sources indicate that in July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) paved the way for Russia's full return to international sport by ending its recommendation that Russian athletes be allowed to compete as neutrals, without their flag, colors or anthems. The IOC also mentioned Russian teams should be allowed to return to international competition.

Several major Olympic sports, such as swimming and gymnastics, have already fully reinstated Russia, despite the country's ongoing attacks on Ukraine.

"It makes no sense to me," Heraskevych said.

However, in recent weeks there has been a growing European pushback against the easing of Russia's sporting isolation.

Among the catalysts was a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) to overturn a ban on Russia in international ice hockey. That prompted seven European countries to say they would refuse to play against Russia, while Germany, at one point, said withdrawing as host of next year's men's world championship was an option.

The dispute over the CAS ruling drew a response from the Kremlin.

"It is a flagrant violation of the Olympic Charter [the IOC's rulebook] and leads toward the destruction of Olympism as a whole," Russian President Vladimir Putin remarked in China last week.

"Sport, like art, should bring people together.".

Meanwhile, a group of Nordic and Baltic countries want the EU to go even further, pushing for an immediate EU-wide visa ban on all Russian athletes.

"The matter is too urgent to wait until [new visa rules] enter into force," the leaders of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Sweden wrote in a November 23 letter to von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa.

"From my perspective, the IOC is in a very big crisis," Heraskevych mentioned, referencing the European pushback.

Blanket bans could have a huge effect on qualifying events in Europe for the 2028 Los Angeles Summer Olympics.

Under its president, Kirsty Coventry, the IOC has sought to bring Russia, an Olympic powerhouse, back in from the cold. Coventry has argued that athletes shouldn't be punished for the actions of their governments, and the IOC has strengthened its political neutrality rules in the Olympic Charter.

However, Heraskevych takes exception to the idea that sport should be kept out of politics.

"We are not living in a bubble," he stated.

"Already more than 800 people who were part of the sport family in Ukraine were killed. Ukrainian hockey stadiums, Ukrainian swimming pools, anything related to sports have also been attacked. So we cannot separate sport and politics in Ukraine. The same way Russian sport is involved in politics.".

Recent findings suggest that critics have accused Coventry of cozying up to Russia. In September, it emerged that she had written a letter to Mikhail Degtyarev, Russia's sports minister and president of the Russian Olympic Committee, wishing him luck ahead of an international sports forum.

Degtyarev has been sanctioned by the EU. The IOC has declined to comment on the letter but not denied its existence.

Heraskevych mentioned he was not "angry" with any particular Russian athlete, and even floated the idea of a team of Russian refugees.

"I am not against peaceful athletes competing," he said.

"They should be part of competition only if they are part of a refugee team. So, if they have refugee status in another country, and if they condemn the war that Russia started in Ukraine.".

Recent findings suggest that merino Wool May be a super fiber well worth owning, but it isn't cheap. Right now, one of my favorite merino wool companies, Unbound Merino, is having its once-a-year sale. Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale is a great chance to round out your travel wardrobe with some excellent merino wool. Better hurry though, unlike most sales this time of year, Unbound Merino's Black Friday sale ends tonight.

From casual, everyday T-shirts, to underwear, socks, and great merino travel pants, Unbound has a little something for everyone. We've combed through the site and found a few of our favorite deals. Be sure to see our guide to the Best Merino Wool T-shirts, Best Merino Wool Clothes, and the Best Base Layers for more great merino wool options.

What’s So Great About Merino Wool?

It has been revealed that merino wool is great because you're stealing a sheep's ability to keep itself warm or cool based on the temperatures it's in. This is a process often referred to as thermoregulation. Merino sheep have thinner, softer wool than what most people think of when they think of wool. The sheep evolved this soft coat to keep them comfortable across a wide range of temperatures. The result is a fabric that's comfortable to wear next to your skin. For the softest tees, look for fabrics that are either superfine or ultrafine—anything 17 µm or higher—like Unbound's T-shirts.

It has been revealed that wool is sustainable, too. One sheep can produce 4 to 5 pounds of wool per year. While cotton has its place, and so does the occasional synthetic garment, merino wool is a remarkable fabric that's the cornerstone of my wardrobe. I don't think you can have too many merino pieces in your closet, but they’re not cheap, which is why we're featuring these deals.

What’s So Great About Unbound Merino?

It has been revealed that I like Unbound's T-shirts because they're 100 percent merino wool, no synthetics involved. That means all the antibacterial, odor-resistant, moisture-wicking, temperature-regulating goodness of merino wool … just works. I've found Unbound's T-shirts in particular to be very quick-drying and wrinkle resistant, two of the reasons I think they're the best merino T-shirts for travel. The company's pants also have a very high wool percentage (95 percent), and they roll up nicely, making them very packable. Do you need special travel clothing? No, but Unbound's merino wool is naturally odor-resistant, which means you need fewer pieces in your bag. The company also offers a 30-day guarantee. If you don't like it, you can send it back.

Most merino products come with care instructions. Unbound Merino's T-shirts should be washed cold with like colors, then laid flat to dry. Whatever you do, don't bleach them and don't tumble dry them. The latter is especially destructive. I do it to every wool T-shirt I test, and it makes me sad, but I know some of you won't listen and will do it anyway, so I have to know what happens so I can warn you. Don't tumble dry. Just put it on a drying rack. It doesn't take more than a day. Seriously, you just spent $80 (on sale!) on a T-shirt; take care of it. Properly cared for, high-quality merino clothing like Unbound's is incredibly durable and will last for years. Throw it in the dryer and the pilling starts almost immediately.

Do I always lay them flat to dry? No. When traveling I usually hand-wash in the sink and then drape them over the shower curtain rod to dry, which hasn't seemed to have much negative impact. The problems with hanging wool to dry is that it will stretch out from the water weight. This is particularly true with 100 percent merino, like Unbound's T-shirts.

Industry observers note that I've never had a problem storing merino in my closet between wears, but for long-term storage, I recommend you take precautions against moths, which are notorious for eating holes in wool. I have lost merino garments to moths. I make sure to wash and thoroughly dry whatever I am storing, then I seal it in a compression bag. Another option is to put your merino garment in a cotton bag or otherwise wrap it in cotton and then put it in a plastic bin. It's very notable to make sure that the garment is completely dry before using any of these storage methods; otherwise your wool will smell musty and moldy. Other options include storing your garment in a cedar chest, which is a good natural deterrent for moths, or use moth traps or lavender sachets, which will repel the moths.

Unbound Merino (Unbound Merino Women’s).

In a recent development, unbound's T-shirts were my introduction to the brand, and they're still one of my favorite merino T-shirts. This T-shirt is incredibly soft, and because it's 100 percent merino wool, it'll stay odor-free for ages—as long as five or six days in my testing (depending on local temps, what you're doing, etc). Unbound's crew neck merino T-shirt has a relaxed, casual cut. It's not going for the technical look you'll get from many outdoor brands. It's also lightweight and packs down to a tiny ball, which is perfect if you're looking to simplify down to one bag. (Really, is there any other way to travel?).

The final thing I love about these is how fast they dry. In most climates, you can give it a wash in the sink at night, roll it up in a towel, wring it dry, lay it out flat, and it'll be dry by morning. If they have a downside, it's that Unbound's T-shirts do need to be babied a little. To help them last a long time I recommend hand washing and line-drying. Also note that while I like the merino crew neck, the V-neck is also on sale for $88 ($10 off).

In a recent development, unbound's merino travel pants are a light and comfortable merino blend, with plenty of stretch and freedom of moment, thanks to the 5 percent elastane. These have a more formal look, what you might call slacks if you are a certain type of person. You might even be able to pull off going to office in them, but I'd sooner chew my leg off than work in an office, so I don't really know. I can say I've worn them to nice restaurants without a second look, and yet they don't scream “I've got money” when you're stumbling back to your hotel room in Prague at 4 am.

In a recent development, as you would expect from anything Unbound makes, these pack down fantastically small. You can pack two pairs of these for every pair of jeans. Again, for serious travelers looking to live out of a single carry-on bag, that's huge. The only downside is that these are on the thin side, not something you'd want to wear alone in cold climates. If you're like me and have to deal with winter, throw a good base layer underneath them and you'll be fine. The slim fit pant is also on sale if that's more your style.

One of the best ways to save at the Unbound Merino Black Friday sale is to go for a bundle. I like this 1-Pack bundle, which gets you a T-shirt, underwear and socks for $125. There are quite a few other bundles as well, including the T-shirt 3-pack for $240 ($54 off) which is $20 cheaper than buying three T-shirts on sale, the boxer briefs pack for $75 ($15 off), and the sock 3-pack which is a steal at just $40 ($38 off).

Recent findings suggest that unbound's merino boxers are warm without being hot, great at wicking moisture, and capable of several wears without undue odors. 84 percent merino wool, 12 percent nylon, and 4 percent spandex, for a soft, stretchy, comfortable fit. They're 180 GSM (see our merino guide for exactly what GSM means), which makes them nice and light. The inseam here is 5.5 inches, and there's no tag, which is nice. The women's underwear is also on sale.

Industry observers note that I prefer the short-sleeve T-shirts, but if you want a long sleeve, this is the T-shirt for you. It's essentially Unbound's short sleeve T-shirt, just long sleeve. All the same descriptions apply here, and many of the same multipack bundles are available. You can grab a 2-pack of long sleeve merino tees for $190 ($40 off).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, stretching over 200,000 square kilometers across southern Australia, the vast, flat plains of the Nullarbor mark one of the world’s largest regions of limestone. It formed when an ancient shallow sea retreated some 14 million years ago.

Ultimately, this led to the familiar dry landscape of today, which has acted as a significant barrier for plants, animals, and poorly adapted colonial Victorian-era explorers who described it as “the sort of place one gets into in bad dreams”.

In a recent development, in contrast, the Mirning People of the Nullarbor and Great Australian Bight have lived for tens of thousands of years on this southern margin. They have watched the landscapes change and sea levels fall and rise with the build-up and collapse of the last ice age about 20,000 years ago.

In a recent development, to an untrained eye the Nullarbor Plain appears deceptively simple and featureless. However, beneath the immense plain lies a remarkable, largely hidden underground world.

Over millions of years, water has eaten away at the limestone and created complex cave networks that can extend for kilometers underground. Sadly, the caves remain poorly understood, partly because they’re only really known and accessible where they breach the surface.

Our new study, published in Communications Earth & Environment, reveals a new way to track these cave systems even when they are deeply buried. Our work helps explain the formation of previously mysterious, shallow trench features on the Nullarbor. It also provides a new way to identify hidden caves elsewhere – even beyond our own planet.

Scattered across the Nullarbor are tell-tale signs of its vulnerability to being dissolved – small cave openings and shallow depressions.

In a recent development, but there are also structures of previously unknown origin and significance: long (up to 20 km), shallow (a few meters) trenches that trend roughly north-south. They’re almost invisible from the ground, but we can clearly see them in modern digital landscape models.

Sources indicate that these shallow trenches look somewhat like flat-bottomed valleys, but they were not carved by rivers. They begin and end abruptly and are not connected to existing rivers or drainage networks that extend into the upland areas around the Nullarbor.

They also lack typical river branching patterns and the sediments within them don’t show any evidence of being deposited from flowing water.

To understand how these strange structures formed, we combined several investigative techniques.

According to recent reports, first, we mapped the trenches using drone and aerial photography, as well as detailed satellite-based digital landscape models. Then the layers of soil and rock were measured in boreholes and caves.

Finally, we used specialized geophysical techniques to “see” inside the Earth, somewhat similar to the way an X-ray enables us to see our internal body structures from the outside.

The work demonstrated that the shallow surface trenches sit above deep zones of broken rock, and in places line up with known cave systems and sinkholes.

This means the trenches are mere muted surface expressions of deeply buried cave systems. These systems are slowly, over millions of years, “collapsing upwards” through the overlying rock layers to reach the surface.

The results of this work will change how scientists interpret cave landscapes globally. It highlights that to explain the surface structures we see, we must look deeper than we might think.

Understanding where voids may exist underground can be notable for planning both surface (buildings, roads) and subsurface (tunnels, sewers) engineering works, mitigating geological hazards, and accessing and protecting groundwater resources.

Pockmarked karst landscapes (where rocks are dissolved by water, resulting in caves and sinkholes) represent 15% of the ice-free Earth’s surface and supply water to 10–25% of the global population.

More fundamentally, caves are crucial scientific archives. Because caves are sheltered from surface weathering and erosion processes, they can preserve snapshots of ancient environments and ecosystems that would otherwise be lost to time.

Furthermore, they may host an array of strange and vulnerable life-forms that have evolved and adapted in isolation. These are some of the least studied organisms on Earth.

To learn more, we must first locate the cave structures. And the results of our study could be very important in this regard.

The implications of this upcoming work even extend beyond our own planet. Because caves offer a stable environment and shelter from damaging space radiation, they provide promising exploration sites for life on other planets.

Mapping of planetary surfaces within our Solar System has identified numerous potential caves, including some thought to be related to karst on Mars.

The Nullarbor’s dry, stable surface is an excellent analogue to help locate the subtle surface fingerprints of hidden cave systems on planets that now lack a dynamic water-cycle – such as Mars. Even if the caves are barren of life, they could be attractive bases for future human explorers.

Sources indicate that how many other apparently simple landscapes around the world or on other planets are concealing large cave systems underneath? We don’t yet know, but the trenches we studied are unlikely to be unique. Similar subtle landforms are likely to have been overlooked elsewhere, too.

Sometimes the most remarkable discoveries are waiting in understated but plain view, in landscapes we think we already understand.

Webb from La Trobe University; Uroš Stepišnik, Matej Dolenec, Primož Miklavc, Tomislav Popit and Andrej Šmuc from the University of Ljubljana; and Jian-xin Zhao from The University of Queensland.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health.
  • In a recent development, astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency.

Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health.

In a recent development, astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space. To help understand how crop production works in microgravity, NASA is launching a novel space crops experiment.

The latest prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing safe, nutritious, and reliable crop production systems for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Knowledge gained from the space crop production system also could help inform agricultural practices such as vertical farming and indoor growing systems.

Researchers will use this investigation to validate the system’s water delivery and volume optimization technology aboard the space station.

A precision health investigation is the next step toward enabling long-duration studies of human brain tissues in space.

The research builds on a previous investigation that sent small, lab-grown models of the human brain, called miBrains, to the space station. This experiment will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid needed to keep the tissues alive.

Researchers could use the findings to help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. It also may advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth.

NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomena under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

Breaking: Scientists discover signs of a hidden extinction crisis deep beneath the ocean

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest genetic findings reveal that marine animals living deep beneath the surface of the Gulf may be at greater risk of extinction than scientists once thought.
  • It has been revealed that as biodiversity declines around the world, the deep ocean has largely been regarded as a natural sanctuary where marine life is better protected from environmental threats.
  • Drawing on 12 years of genetic data, researchers identified concerning signs of extinction risk in five marine species that inhabit waters hundreds of meters below the surface of the Gulf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest genetic findings reveal that marine animals living deep beneath the surface of the Gulf may be at greater risk of extinction than scientists once thought.

It has been revealed that as biodiversity declines around the world, the deep ocean has largely been regarded as a natural sanctuary where marine life is better protected from environmental threats. However, fresh research led by scientists at Florida International University (FIU) is challenging that assumption.

Drawing on 12 years of genetic data, researchers identified concerning signs of extinction risk in five marine species that inhabit waters hundreds of meters below the surface of the Gulf. Their findings suggest that a biodiversity crisis may also be developing in one of Earth's most extensive and poorly understood environments.

It has been revealed that the research was led by FIU marine scientist Pedro A. Peres of the Bracken-Grissom Lab and focused on three species of lanternfish and two species of deep-sea shrimp collected between 2011 and 2023.

The team examined DNA from 486 specimens to determine how the populations have changed over time and assess their ability to withstand future environmental stress. According to Peres, few studies have investigated changes in the genetic makeup of deep-sea animals over an extended period.

Hidden Genetic Signs of Extinction Risk.

It has been revealed that every species examined displayed genetic characteristics linked to a greater risk of extinction, Peres said. One species of lanternfish, Diaphus dumerilii, experienced an approximately 8% reduction in genetic diversity in just 12 years. This loss matches or exceeds declines recorded in some threatened and endangered animals across considerably longer timespans.

Recent findings suggest that all five species also had relatively small effective population sizes. Rather than indicating that the animals are necessarily scarce, this finding suggests that only a limited proportion of individuals are passing their genetic information on to subsequent generations.

Sources indicate that "This challenges the idea that deep-sea species are naturally more resilient because they occupy such vast environments," Peres mentioned. "It indicates how much we can miss when we look only at population abundance without considering their genetic diversity and long-term viability.".

In a recent development, genetic variation plays a fundamental role in determining whether a species can survive environmental changes, explained Heather Bracken-Grissom, assistant director of the Institute of Environment's Coastlines and Oceans Division. Bracken-Grissom, a co-author of the study, has led research exploring the genetic health and resilience of animals living in the deep ocean.

According to recent reports, "Genetic diversity provides the variation populations need to adapt to changing conditions, resist disease and recover from environmental disturbances," she said. "When that diversity disappears, a species can also lose the ability to withstand future threats.".

Climate Change Could Dramatically Shrink Deep-Sea Habitats.

The team also used climate models to estimate how environmental conditions in the Gulf could affect the availability of suitable deep-sea habitats by 2050 and 2100. The projections indicate that four of the five species could face substantial habitat losses, potentially reaching 70%.

Peres noted that these results are especially troubling given the longstanding belief that the enormous habitats and widespread geographic distributions of deep-sea animals allow them to maintain large, resilient populations.

In a recent development, the discoveries also prompt new questions about the long-term environmental impact of the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill. Earlier research revealed considerable reductions in deep-sea animal populations in the aftermath of the disaster.

While the scientists have not established a direct link between the oil spill and the genetic changes they observed, their results indicate that environmental disruptions could have repercussions extending well beyond their initial impact.

"Our results suggest some deep-sea populations may have already been genetically vulnerable before the Deepwater Horizon oil spill," Peres said. "This has vital implications for understanding the consequences of environmental disturbances. Events such as oil spills may affect populations that already have limited genetic resilience.".

An Urgent Need To Monitor Deep-Sea Biodiversity.

It has been revealed that the study, which also includes co-authors Keith Sellers of FIU and Tracey T. Sutton of Nova Southeastern University, highlights the importance of examining the genetic health of marine populations. Monitoring changes in DNA over time could help scientists identify threats to species survival that conventional population surveys fail to detect.

"This study serves as a wake-up call for the scientific community," Peres said, "highlighting the urgent need to integrate genetic monitoring into biodiversity assessments and emphasizing the importance of long-term monitoring to better understand and detect changes in marine populations over time.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The H3 Podcast has come to an end.

On Monday, Hila Klein announced on the show's Instagram account that she had "made the difficult decision to stop working on the new show." She had been developing a crew-led version of the podcast since her estranged husband and co-host, Ethan Klein, was pushed out of it last month after she revealed his affair.

Industry observers note that "I've come to realize that I can't continue down this path while also giving myself the space I need to heal and protect my mental health," she wrote. "Right now, I need to focus on myself, my healing, and what's best for me and my kids.".

Recent findings suggest that the announcement closes out a month-long fallout that began on Oct. 22. That day, Ethan said on Instagram Stories that the podcast was going on "indefinite hiatus." Hours later, Hila posted that he had been having an affair for more than six months. As Mashable previously reported, the crew said in a statement that they would not keep working with Ethan "involved or profiting in any way." Ethan said he was working to give up his financial stakes in the podcast and in the couple's businesses, including the clothing brand Teddy Fresh.

Industry observers note that complex reported that Hila filed for divorce on Nov. 2, listing their separation date as Oct. 13. The couple married in 2012 and share three children.

Recent findings suggest that since the news broke, multiple crew members have spoken out. On the show's Discord, longtime producer GirlWithAMicrophone (GWAM) said she would not work on a project with the rest of the crew. She thanked Hila for giving them "a shot during all this turmoil.".

Recent findings suggest that producer AB Ayad suggested on X that the obstacles were bigger than any one person. "There are certain people involved that were never gonna allow us to continue doing the show together," he wrote, adding, "I give Hila a lot of credit that she was able to do what she even did.".

Recent findings suggest that beyond the H3 Podcast, Ethan co-hosted Frenemies with Trisha Paytas, which became one of YouTube's most talked-about indicates before it ended acrimoniously in 2021. He later started the political show Leftovers with Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, which ended in 2023 over disagreements about Israel and the war in Gaza.

Since the announcement of the show ending, Ethan has broken his weeks-long silence. On Tuesday, in a series of Instagram Stories, he called the affair "the ultimate betrayal" to his wife and to the show's audience. He also remarked that "the show ending is entirely my fault.".

However, he didn't rule out a comeback. "I will probably be back, but when and how, I can't tell you," he wrote, hinting at a solo show or a fresh project.

Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (645 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that more than a mile below the surface of the Red Sea, researchers from the University of Miami (UM) Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science discovered rare deep-sea brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, a northern extension of the Red Sea.
  • The discovery was made by Sam Purkis, professor and chair of the UM Department of Marine Geosciences, and his colleagues in collaboration with OceanX.
  • Industry observers note that "Until we understand the limits of life on Earth, it will be difficult to determine if alien planets can host any living beings," stated Purkis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that more than a mile below the surface of the Red Sea, researchers from the University of Miami (UM) Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science discovered rare deep-sea brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, a northern extension of the Red Sea. These unusually salty underwater lakes could provide clues to how Earth's oceans formed millions of years ago and help guide the search for life on other planets.

The discovery was made by Sam Purkis, professor and chair of the UM Department of Marine Geosciences, and his colleagues in collaboration with OceanX. The researchers located the pools at a depth of more than one mile (1,770 meters) using a remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV) deployed from the OceanXplorer, an advanced research vessel equipped to investigate some of the least accessible environments on Earth.

Industry observers note that "Until we understand the limits of life on Earth, it will be difficult to determine if alien planets can host any living beings," stated Purkis. "Our discovery of a rich community of microbes that survive in extreme environments can help trace the limits of life on Earth and can be applied to the search for life elsewhere in our solar system and beyond.".

Life thrives in extreme underwater lakes.

Brine pools rank among the harshest environments on our planet. Their waters contain exceptionally high concentrations of salt, feature unusual chemical conditions, and are completely devoid of oxygen. Despite these seemingly inhospitable conditions, the pools support abundant microbial life. Previous research on microbes inhabiting Red Sea brine pools has even identified biologically active molecules with potential anticancer properties.

The findings, published in Communications Earth & Environment, mark the first documented discovery of brine pools in the Gulf of Aqaba. Remarkably, the researchers nearly missed them.

It has been revealed that "We were very lucky," said Purkis. "The discovery came in the last five minutes of the ten-hour ROV dive that we could dedicate to this project.".

Hidden records of ancient tsunamis and earthquakes.

Beyond their biological significance, the pools serve as natural archives of the region's geological history. Situated relatively close to the coastline, their extremely salty waters and absence of oxygen help preserve evidence of tsunamis, flash floods, and earthquakes that occurred in the Gulf of Aqaba thousands of years ago. Regional tectonic activity has produced numerous faults and fractures across the seabed in this part of the gulf.

Earlier in 2022, Purkis and his colleagues uncovered evidence of a 500-year-old underwater landslide that likely generated a substantial tsunami. Understanding the region's history of such events could have important implications for coastal development in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.

The study, titled "Discovery of the deep-sea NEOM Brine Pools in the Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea," was published on June 27, 2022, in Communications Earth & Environment.

The research team included Sam J. Purkis, Hannah Shernisky, Peter K. Swart, Arash Sharifi, Amanda Oehlert, Gaëlle Duchâtellier, James Klaus, Gregor P. Eberli, Larry Peterson, and Graham Kolodziej from the UM Rosenstiel School; Fabio Marchese and Francesca Benzoni from King Abdullah University of Science and Technology's Red Sea Research Center; Giovanni Chimienti from the University of Bari Aldo Moro in Italy; Andrew Craig and Mattie Rodrigue from OceanX; Jürgen Titschack from MARUM -- Center for Marine Environmental Sciences in Germany; and Ameer Abdulla from NEOM.

NEOM, a tech giant developing the Saudi Arabian coastline, provided funding for the four-week research expedition aboard the OceanXplorer.

Watch the NEOM OceanX documentary about the discovery: https://youtu.be/bWNftnYDx9c.

Latest Update: Retail turnarounds are taking hold just in time for the holiday season

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Once-struggling retailers are entering the holiday quarter with improved performance and sales momentum as turnaround efforts begin to resonate with shoppers.
  • A handful of earnings reports on Tuesday pointed to a mix of factors behind the strong results, including a resilient consumer, stronger execution and demand for the right products at the right price.
  • Kohl's reported comparable sales growth of 1.2% for the period ended Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Once-struggling retailers are entering the holiday quarter with improved performance and sales momentum as turnaround efforts begin to resonate with shoppers.

A handful of earnings reports on Tuesday pointed to a mix of factors behind the strong results, including a resilient consumer, stronger execution and demand for the right products at the right price.

Kohl's reported comparable sales growth of 1.2% for the period ended Oct. 31 and raised its full-year outlook as CEO Michael Bender remarked customers "have remained resilient" but are "migrating to value with their purchases.".

He tied improvement to the organization's work on product assortment, store experience and value.

Best Buy also on Tuesday posted its highest comparable sales growth in five years, at 6.1%, which prompted the electronics retailer to raise its full-year outlook.

"We have a tremendous amount of momentum," CEO Jason Bonfig told CNBC in an interview. "The fact that we saw pretty much broad-based growth across almost all of our categories is a lot of momentum that we're very excited about.".

The manufacturer also credited execution, market share gains and a compelling product cycle alongside growing customer demand.

Sources indicate that at Dick's Sporting Goods, quarterly comparable sales rose 2.6% at the core business and 0.5% at Foot Locker. CEO Lauren Hobart remarked "all income demographics grew" and the organization "didn't see trade-down from best to better or better to good.".

Sources indicate that she similarly pointed to new products and market share gains within the category as contributing to the strong quarter. She also highlighted continued improvement at Foot Locker.

All three companies have been undergoing efforts to boost sales and get the right products on shelves to meet customer demand.

Target, likewise undergoing revitalization efforts, last week reported comparable sales growth of 5.6% in the third quarter, fueled by a 5% increase in comparable traffic. The retailer raised its full-year outlook.

CEO Michael Fiddelke at the time called the traffic gain "a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often.".

Even Gap CEO Richard Dickson told CNBC the organization has moved from "rebuild mode" to "turnaround mode" at its Old Navy banner, a sign of progress, albeit not a broad-based portfolio recovery.

Michael Baker, a retail analyst at D.A. Davidson, told CNBC he sees both a resilient consumer and organization-specific improvements as driving sector strength.

"Retail sales have been more resilient than most think," Baker stated. His analysis revealed retail sales, excluding autos and gas, rose 5.1% in the third quarter on a nonseasonally adjusted basis — the strongest quarter since the pandemic.

But he cautioned that growth appears to be coming more from transaction size than traffic, with inflation, promotions and higher units per transaction driving up spend.

In a recent development, dollar Tree, which reported better-than-expected earnings on Tuesday morning, posted a 3.8% increase to traffic, accelerating from 0.4% growth in the prior quarter, suggesting more shoppers may be bargain hunting. Comparable sales at the retailer increased 4.6% during the period.

Recent findings suggest that "Consumers are under pressure, and they are increasingly selective about where and how they spend," said Dollar Tree CEO Michael Creedon on the firm's earnings call. "When under pressure, shoppers prioritize value and buy closer to need.".

Comparable sales of everyday essentials rose 8.9% at Dollar Tree stores in the third quarter, while sales of nonessential items were essentially flat, the manufacturer stated.

— CNBC's Laya Neelakandan contributed to this report.

#150633. For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1250 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

For decades, scientists may have misunderstood how brain cells work

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even before a fresh neuroscience study appeared in Nature, its preliminary version had been downloaded more than 11,000 times.
  • Do neurons operate like individual tools, such as hammers and saws, each designed for a particular job?
  • Researchers at Columbia's Zuckerman Institute examined an extensive collection of mouse brain recordings gathered through an international collaboration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even before a fresh neuroscience study appeared in Nature, its preliminary version had been downloaded more than 11,000 times. The research addresses one of the oldest and most hotly debated questions in neuroscience: how specialized are the individual cells that make up the brain?

Do neurons operate like individual tools, such as hammers and saws, each designed for a particular job? Or are they more like Swiss Army knives, capable of handling many different tasks?

Researchers at Columbia's Zuckerman Institute examined an extensive collection of mouse brain recordings gathered through an international collaboration. Their analysis revealed that while some neurons are indeed specialists, most appear capable of responding to many different kinds of information.

"We have to move away from this image of the brain as a machine made of gears, with every gear having an exact purpose that we can attach a label to," noted Stefano Fusi, PhD, a principal investigator at Columbia's Zuckerman Institute, a member of the Kavli Institute for Brain Science and the paper's co-senior author. "The brain doesn't work like that. Instead, most neurons can display a huge diversity of responses, and this can help the brain solve a huge number of different tasks.".

The discovery could help explain how the brain achieves its remarkable ability to perform complex tasks. It could also provide a foundation for understanding what happens when brain function is disrupted and identifying ways to restore it.

Revisiting a Decades-Old Neuroscience Debate.

Recent findings suggest that the question of whether neurons are specialists or generalists "is an old, notable question, and one which researchers have really strong opinions on," noted Lorenzo Posani, PhD, the study's co-lead author and a principal investigator at the Paris Brain Institute and France's CNRS. Posani conducted the research while working at Columbia's Zuckerman Institute.

It has been revealed that scientists have long known that the brain contains distinct regions responsible for functions such as sight and smell. This organization suggests that individual neurons might also have narrowly defined roles. However, the brain is also an extraordinarily powerful biological computer capable of adapting to countless situations, raising the possibility that its individual neurons are similarly versatile.

Recent findings suggest that one reason the debate has persisted is that researchers have approached the question under widely different experimental conditions, Posani explained. Previous studies examined different animal species, investigated different parts of the brain, or required animals to complete different activities. Unsurprisingly, their conclusions often conflicted. Some experiments identified highly specialized neurons, while others revealed cells with much broader capabilities.

A Massive Study of 43 Brain Regions.

To obtain a more consistent picture of neural activity, the researchers focused exclusively on mice performing the same type of task. They also examined numerous brain regions simultaneously, drawing on datasets considerably larger than those typically used in neuroscience research.

The recordings, collected by the International Brain Laboratory consortium, captured the activity of individual neurons across 43 regions of the mouse cerebral cortex.

The analysis revealed an key distinction. Neurons in primary sensory regions, including areas responsible for processing visual information, tended to exhibit more specialized responses. Across other regions, however, individual neurons displayed a considerably wider range of activity. The overall findings suggest that generalists, rather than specialists, dominate much of the cortex.

Recent findings suggest that "We're not saying that there are no specialized neurons," stated Dr. Fusi, who is also a professor of neuroscience at Columbia's Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons and a member of Columbia's Center for Theoretical Neuroscience. "We're saying they are the exceptions. They're not the rule.".

Most Neurons Are Versatile in Different Ways.

Despite the versatility of individual neurons, the brain retains a distinct regional organization. By examining how a neuron responded during a particular task, the scientists could identify with surprising accuracy which functional module it belonged to. Yet membership in a particular brain module did not generally mean that a neuron was limited to a single function.

It has been revealed that "For example, compare this to maps of voter opinions," Dr. Posani said. "There are clear clusters where people generally vote the same way. But when you zoom in, you see mixes of opinions.".

In a recent development, the researchers also uncovered another striking feature of neural activity. Not only do most neurons handle multiple kinds of information, but their patterns of activity rarely mirror those of other neurons.

"Each is versatile in its own way," says study co-lead author Shuqi Wang, a doctoral student at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne in Switzerland. According to Wang, this diversity helps give the brain its flexibility and impressive computational abilities.

The Secret Behind the Brain's Computing Power.

The researchers propose that the versatility of neurons allows individual brain cells to represent several types of information at once. For example, a neuron might respond to both the color of an object, such as red or black, and its shape, such as a circle or square.

Working together, groups of neurons can form what scientists call "high-dimensional" representations of information. These representations capture multiple characteristics simultaneously, allowing the brain to distinguish a red circle from a black square, for instance.

Sources indicate that this arrangement gives groups of neurons considerable flexibility in how they process incoming information and generate responses. Rather than requiring an entirely separate neural representation for every newly introduced task, the brain can draw on existing combinations of neural activity.

"You can reuse these high-dimensional representations for lots of different tasks," Dr. Fusi said.

Rethinking How Scientists Study the Brain.

Sources indicate that the findings also have significant implications for how neuroscientists investigate brain function. Because a single neuron can carry information about several different variables, determining precisely what it represents by examining its activity alone can be extremely difficult.

A clearer picture emerges when scientists analyze the combined activity of many neurons, much as the brain itself processes information through populations of cells.

This represents an key change in perspective for the neuroscience community, "which for decades focused on one neuron at a time, discarding all neurons whose responses could not be understood," Dr. Fusi said.

Do Human Brain Cells Work the Same Way?

The researchers are now collaborating with Ueli Rutishauser's research group at Caltech to determine whether human neurons exhibit similar patterns of versatility.

They also hope to establish whether the degree of specialization among neurons changes depending on the particular demands of a task.

Recent findings suggest that "There is still a lot to discover," Dr. Fusi noted.

The paper, "Rarely categorical and highly separable: how neural representations change along the cortical hierarchy," was published in Nature.

The full list of authors includes Lorenzo Posani, Shuqi Wang, Samuel P. Muscinelli, Liam Paninski and Stefano Fusi.

Industry observers note that the research received funding from the National Institutes of Health (RF1AG080818, U19NS123716), the Simons Foundation, the Kavli Foundation, the Gatsby Foundation (GAT3708), and the Swartz Foundation. Additional support was provided by the National Science Foundation and the DoD Office of the Under Secretary of Defense (R&E) under Cooperative Agreement PHY-2229929 (the NSF AI Institute for Artificial and Natural Intelligence). Dr. Posani received additional support through the NIH 1K99MH135166-01 grant.

Materials provided by The Zuckerman Institute at Columbia University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#150630. The tiny BSW is a party in crisis, as it is set to hand the far-right AfD power in eastern Germany

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1006 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

The tiny BSW is a party in crisis, as it is set to hand the far-right AfD power in eastern Germany

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that this fledgling party has experienced many highs and lows in quick succession.
  • Since October 2026, the acronym BSW has instead stood for theAlliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason.
  • It has been revealed that even more painful for the BSW was its defeat in the German general election in February 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this fledgling party has experienced many highs and lows in quick succession. Launched in January 2024, it was named the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) to capitalize on the high profile and momentum of its founder, a former communist who had just exited the socialist Left party.

Since October 2026, the acronym BSW has instead stood for theAlliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason. In the past 34 months the newcomer party celebrated election successes at the European Parliament level and in German state elections. In the eastern states of Brandenburg and Thuringia, the party even took part in governing coalitions; however, both of these collapsed relatively quickly.

It has been revealed that even more painful for the BSW was its defeat in the German general election in February 2025. The party failed to gain the 5% share of votes required to enter parliament, by less than 10,000 votes. With that, it was denied the country's most notable political stage and took the matter to court, demanding a complete recount.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But Germany's Constitutional Court dismissed the BSW's election challenge as inadmissible, pointing to a lack of evidence.

"Simply insinuating the possibility of voting errors or expressing an unproven assumption does not meet the requirements for claiming an electoral mistake," the court explained.

The court's decision was published about a week before the party's federal conference is due to be held in Dresden, the capital of the eastern state of Saxony.

"Germany's election scrutiny process resembles that of a 'banana republic'," was the angry reaction of former party leader Sahra Wagenknecht, who stepped back from frontline leadership of her eponymous party in December 2025. Since then, she has led its commission on fundamental values.

In a recent development, one of her successors at the top of the BSW is European Parliament lawmaker Fabio De Masi. In his view, the decision of the Constitutional Court was a "black day for democracy in Germany.".

Fellow co-leader Amira Mohamed Ali did not want to accept the rejected recount.

"It remains unclear whether the Bundestag is correctly composed and whether the approximately 2.5 million BSW voters have unjustly been deprived of their parliamentary representation," she stated.

According to recent reports, the disappointment at the failure to enter the Bundestag runs deep. The party has not recovered from this setback. It again failed to win representation in 4 out of 5 state parliaments in elections this year, albeit narrowly.

In Baden-Württemberg and Rhineland-Palatinate, as well as in the city-state of Hamburg in 2025, the BSW received less than 2%. This clearly demonstrates that it is politically irrelevant in the western German states.

They find themselves in the spotlight, however,  because of the role they are set to play in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the BSW got 5.3% of the vote in September.

Despite being the smallest party in that state parliament, they are set to play a pivotal role. They are the only political party that has indicated a readiness to help the election winner, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), into power.

The AfD, which is classified as right-wing extremist in Saxony-Anhalt by Germany's domestic intelligence agency, won the election with almost 44% of the vote. Although his party does not hold an absolute majority in parliament, lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund wants to be voted Germany's first-ever AfD state premier in December.

According to recent reports, the BSW has not indicated any intention to vote for Siegmund, but if he falls short of winning the absolute majority of 42 votes in the first two rounds of voting, a third round will be held in which a simple majority will suffice to win. The BSW has announced prepares to abstain from that vote. Siegmund would then only need to pick up one more "yes" vote or abstention.

According to recent reports, during the secret ballot for the state parliament speaker, AfD candidate Tobias Rausch received 9 votes more than his party has lawmakers. It is not known exactly who they came from. Alongside the AfD and BSW, there are 4 other parties in the state parliament: the conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), environmentalist Greens, socialist Left Party and center-left Social Democrats (SPD).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The situation in Saxony-Anhalt will be at the center of the party's upcoming conference in Dresden, because the BSW's increasing closeness with the far-right party is highly controversial.

Several BSW members, including board member Christian Leye, criticized this path in a column published in the weekly Die Zeit.

Leye recalled their party's founding consensus: "The clear political demarcation from the AfD.".

He quoted party founder Wagenknecht, who at that time had said: "Of course we will not collude with the AfD.".

"We are starting a party so that all the people who are considering or have voted for the AfD out of anger or disappointment — but not because they are right-wing — have a credible political home," Wagenknecht had continued.

But Wagenknecht has also long argued that the so-called "firewall" policy of mainstream parties refusing to work with the AfD has failed. This is why she is rejecting the idea of entering a mathematically possible governing coalition with the other parties in Saxony-Anhalt.

"We are basically agreed that we neither want to go into coalition with the AfD, nor tolerate them, just as much as we do not want to participate in a firewall coalition," she told German news agency dpa.

How the BSW plans to make its way through this dilemma at its party conference is unclear. Fabio De Masi, who replaced Wagenknecht as co-chair in December 2025, seems well aware of this.

He told German media network RND that dealing with the AfD continued to be like "riding on the edge of a razor blade.".

#150625. Industry News: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (724 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (724 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, men and women appear to be similarly skilled at juggling multiple activities, but upcoming research has uncovered one striking difference.
  • Whether driving, working, doing household chores, or enjoying leisure activities, people frequently find themselves managing several tasks at once or switching between them.
  • With support from the Bial Foundation, researchers André and Diana Szameitat (from Brunel University of London and City St George's, University of London, UK, respectively) set out to determine whether meaningful differences exist in multitasking ability and what might explain the widespread belief that women have an advantage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, men and women appear to be similarly skilled at juggling multiple activities, but upcoming research has uncovered one striking difference. In an experiment designed to recreate the demands of everyday life, men ignored conversational questions more than twice as often as women while performing just as well on the other tasks.

Whether driving, working, doing household chores, or enjoying leisure activities, people frequently find themselves managing several tasks at once or switching between them. Although women are widely believed to be better at multitasking than men, previous research has found only minor and inconsistent differences between the sexes, raising doubts about the accuracy of this popular assumption.

With support from the Bial Foundation, researchers André and Diana Szameitat (from Brunel University of London and City St George's, University of London, UK, respectively) set out to determine whether meaningful differences exist in multitasking ability and what might explain the widespread belief that women have an advantage.

Putting Multitasking Skills to the Test.

In their study, "Men Talk Less Than Women During Multitasking," published in the scientific journal Psychological Research, the researchers developed an experiment involving five different activities. The setup was designed to capture the complexity of everyday multitasking more accurately than most previous studies.

Industry observers note that the first experiment involved 41 men and 37 women. Participants were asked to follow a recipe in a kitchen setting, look up phone numbers, match numbers with letters, watch a slideshow for specific words, and answer conversational questions. A fresh question was posed every 20 seconds (e.g., "Would you rather lose all of your money and valuables or all of the pictures you have ever taken, and why?").

In a recent development, in a second experiment, the researchers recruited 160 observers to determine whether differences in multitasking behavior were noticeable to others. Without being given prior information about the participants or findings, the observers watched video recordings of the experiments and assessed how well the participants performed.

One Surprising Difference Between Men and Women.

Recent findings suggest that men and women achieved comparable results on four of the five activities. Conversation, however, revealed a notable exception. Men left conversational questions unanswered more than twice as often as women. When men did answer, their responses were just as fast and of comparable quality to those given by women.

The researchers suggest that women may, on average, be more inclined to engage in communication during social interactions. However, the study did not directly investigate this possibility, so the explanation should be treated with caution. The results are also consistent with evolutionary theories suggesting that women may have a greater tendency to engage in conversation.

How Conversation Shapes Perceptions of Ability.

The differences in conversational engagement appeared to have a considerable impact on how others judged the participants. Observers rated men as having less control over the activities, performing more poorly, putting in less effort, and being less alert than women. They also perceived men as less happy and as deriving less enjoyment from the experience.

Rather than revealing a broad difference in multitasking ability between men and women, the research points to a much more specific behavioral distinction: men are more likely to leave conversations unanswered when managing several activities simultaneously.

Because conversational engagement is easily noticed by others, this difference may create the impression that men are less effective at multitasking, even when their performance on other activities is comparable to that of women. The findings offer a potential explanation for how the popular stereotype that women are better multitaskers developed and why it continues to persist.

"Taken together, our data confirm that there are no substantial sex differences in cognitive visual-manual tasks, but that significant sex differences do exist in the ability to hold a conversation while multitasking," explains André Szameitat. This is "an ability highly salient in everyday life and, thus, could explain the development of the widespread public stereotype that women are better at multitasking than men," the researcher concludes.

French minister under fire for Playboy magazine cover

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • French government minister Marlene Schiappa has come under fire from members of her own party after appearing on the front cover of Playboy magazine.
  • Schiappa, who has been a government minister since 2017, appeared on the cover of the magazine to accompany a 12-page interview she did on women’s and LGBT rights.
  • Industry observers note that schiappa has been a long-time advocate for women’s rights and was appointed as the country’s first ever Gender Equality Minister in 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

French government minister Marlene Schiappa has come under fire from members of her own party after appearing on the front cover of Playboy magazine.

Schiappa, who has been a government minister since 2017, appeared on the cover of the magazine to accompany a 12-page interview she did on women’s and LGBT rights. Schiappa, who is the current Minister for the Social Economy and French Associations, was photographed for the cover wearing a white dress.

Industry observers note that schiappa has been a long-time advocate for women’s rights and was appointed as the country’s first ever Gender Equality Minister in 2017. In this role, she successfully spearheaded a new sexual harassment law which allows for on the spot fines to be issued to men who catcall, harass or follow women on the street.

Her appearance has drawn criticism from political colleagues including French Prime Minister Elisabeth Borne.

Borne pulled up Schiappa over the cover, telling her it “wasn’t appropriate, especially during this period,” CNN affiliate BFMTV reported Saturday, citing a source close to the prime minister.

France is currently in the throes of a political and social crisis triggered by French President Emmanuel Macron’s move to push ahead with controversial pension reforms despite widespread public opposition.

“We are in the middle of a social crisis, there is the issue of policing, there are people between life and death, and I have the impression of being behind a smoke screen,” Sandrine Rousseau, Green Party politician and fellow women’s rights activist, told BFMTV Friday.

France wracked by more pension protests amid rising violence on the streets.

French politician, Jean Luc Mélenchon who came third in the 2022 presidential elections criticized both Schiappa’s appearance and the decision by French President Emmanuel Macron to give an interview to children’s magazine, Pif Gadget, this week.

In a recent development, “In a country where the President expresses himself in Pif and his minister in Playboy, the problem would be the opposition. France is going off the rails,” Mélenchon tweeted Saturday.

Industry observers note that schiappa responded to her critics in a tweet on Saturday, saying: “Defending the right of women to have control of their bodies, that’s everywhere and all the time. In France, women are free. With all due respect to the detractors and hypocrites.”.

French Interior Minister, Gérald Darmanin came to Schiappa’s defense during an interview with French news channel CNews on Sunday calling her a “woman of character.”.

“I wanted to say that Marlene Schiappa is a courageous female politician who has her character and who has her style which is not mine, but I respect,” he remarked.

Tech Report: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A small fossil discovered in Scotland and regarded for nearly three decades as one of the earliest known reptiles has turned out to be a very different kind of prehistoric animal.
  • According to recent reports, the 345-million-year-old fossil, discovered in 1984, belongs to a species called Westlothiana lizziae.
  • Although the fossil's distorted condition made its anatomy difficult to interpret, researchers widely regarded it as the earliest known amniote adapted to life on land.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A small fossil discovered in Scotland and regarded for nearly three decades as one of the earliest known reptiles has turned out to be a very different kind of prehistoric animal. New research published in Nature is challenging its long-established place in evolutionary history. The study was led by scientists at the American Museum of Natural History and the University of Oxford, working in collaboration with the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility.

According to recent reports, the 345-million-year-old fossil, discovered in 1984, belongs to a species called Westlothiana lizziae. Nicknamed "Lizzie" because of its resemblance to a lizard, the specimen consists of a nearly complete skeleton preserved in two crushed slabs of rock. Early descriptions relied largely on anatomical features visible at the surface, including four limbs with fingers and toes that appeared to have claw-like tips. These characteristics distinguished Westlothiana from many other animals living at the time, whose limbs more closely resembled fins.

Although the fossil's distorted condition made its anatomy difficult to interpret, researchers widely regarded it as the earliest known amniote adapted to life on land. Amniotes are a major group of vertebrates that includes reptiles, birds, and mammals. Following its scientific description in 1990, Westlothiana became an crucial reference point for researchers investigating when and how these animals first evolved.

In a recent development, "Lizzie has been an icon for the early evolution of amniotes for decades," mentioned Xavier Jenkins, a postdoctoral fellow in the Museum's Division of Paleontology and co-lead author of the study. "But when we were finally able to see inside the fossil, we found an animal that looked very different from what we expected.".

Advanced X-Ray Scans Reveal Lizzie's True Identity.

Using powerful X-ray imaging technology at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility in Grenoble, France, the scientists peered beneath the surface of the rock and reconstructed previously inaccessible parts of the animal's anatomy.

What they discovered was strikingly different from the anatomy expected in an early reptile. Lizzie possessed a primitive skull, internal gills containing bone, and a mouth resembling that of a fish, complete with thousands of tiny teeth. Together, these features rule out its previously proposed position within the evolutionary lineage leading to reptiles. Instead of living primarily on land, Westlothiana appears to have been an aquatic or amphibious animal.

It has been revealed that "The surprisingly primitive features of the skull show us that Lizzie was not only not a reptile but belonged to a much more ancient lineage. It turns out looks can be deceiving, and Lizzie lived a completely different lifestyle than we previously thought," mentioned Ben Igielman, co-lead author of the study, who started this research during his graduate work at the University of Oxford.

Reptile-Like Features Evolved in Aquatic Ancestors.

The discovery also changes how scientists understand the origins of several anatomical features traditionally associated with vertebrates adapted to terrestrial environments.

Recent findings suggest that researchers now believe that characteristics such as claws and the arrangement of five digits on each hand and foot, a pattern familiar in reptiles and mammals, had already emerged in earlier animals that were still closely associated with water. These creatures belonged to the evolutionary lineage leading to tetrapods, the broader group of four-limbed vertebrates that encompasses both amphibians and amniotes.

Industry observers note that "This is a big surprise," said study co-author Roger Benson, the Museum's Macaulay Curator of Paleontology. "It indicates that, although we think of amphibians as being more 'primitive' than reptiles today, some of the traits of reptiles were already there in the ancestor of both amphibians and reptiles.".

Ancient Footprints May Tell a Different Story.

Industry observers note that the findings could also have important implications for the interpretation of prehistoric fossil tracks. Recently discovered trackways have been used as evidence that amniotes first appeared during the Devonian Period, more than 359 million years ago.

These ancient impressions record the movements of a four-limbed animal with apparently clawed digits. However, if distant relatives of tetrapods such as Westlothiana also possessed claws, such footprints are no longer sufficient on their own to identify the animals that left them as amniotes.

Some trackways previously attributed to early amniotes may instead have been left by more ancient, amphibious creatures belonging to the evolutionary lineage of tetrapods.

"The broader lesson is that terrestrial-looking traits, such as a reptile-like foot, a weight-bearing forelimb, and claw-like phalanges were not unique features of tetrapods, but rather accumulated piecemeal in their close relatives, in animals that were still living in and out of the water," Jenkins said.

Additional contributors to the study include Jason Head from the University of Cambridge, Vincent Fernandez from the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility, Lucy Roberts from the Natural History Museum, London, and Timothy Smithson from the University Museum of Zoology Cambridge.

The research received funding from the National Science Foundation (grant number EAR-PF 2518154), the National Environment Research Council (grant numbers NE/S000739/1, NE/W007576/1, and NE/L002507/1), and the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (grant number BB/X014819/1).
